Updates `jdx/mise-action` from 5.2.4 to 5.2.9
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/mise-action's releases.

v5.2.9: Maintenance release

This release has no user-facing changes. It updates dependencies and the project's CI.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.8...v5.2.9

v5.2.8: Fix mise install on Windows when MISE_DATA_DIR is on another drive

On Windows, the action can now install mise when MISE_DATA_DIR is on a different drive from the temporary directory. Before this fix, the install failed with EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted.

Fixed

  • Installing mise on Windows no longer fails when MISE_DATA_DIR is on another drive. On hosted windows-2025 runners, the workspace and RUNNER_TEMP are on D:, but the action downloaded mise to os.tmpdir() on C:. If MISE_DATA_DIR pointed into the workspace, moving mise.exe into place failed:

    ##[error]EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted, rename 'C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\mise-action-…\extract\mise\bin\mise.exe' -> 'D:\a\…\tool-cache\mise\bin\mise.exe'

    The action now downloads to RUNNER_TEMP when that variable is set and the directory exists. Otherwise it falls back to the system temp directory. If moving mise.exe, mise-shim.exe or a raw mise binary still crosses drives, the action copies the file and then deletes the original. This also covers self-hosted runners where RUNNER_TEMP is on a different drive from the data directory. Setups that use the default data directory were not affected. If you set TEMP and TMP to ${{ runner.temp }} to work around this, you can remove those settings. (#732 by @​jdx and @​HengYangDS, fixes #730)

New Contributors

  • @​HengYangDS made their first contribution in cff84f4

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.7...v5.2.8

v5.2.7: Retry failed mise downloads with backoff and show the HTTP status

When the action can't download mise, the log now shows the HTTP status and host for each failed attempt. Retries wait longer between attempts, so a short GitHub outage is less likely to fail the job.

Fixed

  • Download failures now show what went wrong, and brief outages are retried for longer. Before this release, a failed mise download logged only The process '/usr/bin/curl' failed with exit code 22 and retried five times with a fixed 2-second wait. From that message you couldn't tell a rate limit from a missing asset or a server error. Each failed attempt now logs the HTTP status and the host that answered:

    Download attempt 1/6 failed: Could not download github.com/…/mise-v2026.10.21-linux-x64.tar.zst (HTTP 503 from github.com). Retrying in 3.4 seconds.

    The wait between attempts doubles from about 2s up to a 30s cap, with random jitter, so the five retries cover roughly a minute. Only transient failures are retried: connection errors and timeouts, and HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx responses. A 404, any other 4xx, or a local file-write error fails at once. The log shows only the host and file name of each URL, never signed query strings or curl/wget stderr. Partial files are deleted before the next attempt. wget now runs with --tries=1, so its own 20-retry default no longer stacks on top of the action's retries. This applies to every download the action makes: the release archive, checksums and the packslip bundle. Checksum and signature verification are unchanged, and there are no new inputs. (#722 by @​jdx, fixes #721)

Changed

  • packslip, which the action uses to verify downloaded mise releases, is updated from 1.11.0 to 1.11.2. This version includes upstream hardening of its verifier checks. (#726)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.6...v5.2.7

v5.2.6: Fix step hanging after a failed cache restore

The action now exits as soon as its work is done. Before this release, a cache restore that failed during the download could leave the step running for up to ten minutes after setup had finished.

Fixed

  • A failed cache restore no longer leaves the step hanging. If the mise cache download failed partway through, for example with getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN, the action logged a warning, installed the tools and saved the cache, then stopped producing output. The step stayed in progress until the job was cancelled or a timer inside @actions/cacheactions/toolkit#2470Error objects now mark the step as failed with their message. Before, they caused an unhandled rejection. (#718 by @​jdx and @​kjanat, fixes #717)

Updates `pydantic-settings` from 2.16.1 to 2.16.3
Release notes

Sourced from pydantic-settings's releases.

v2.16.3

Highlights

This patch release fixes a security issue in the default secrets source, a regression from 2.14.2 that dropped nested secrets on Kubernetes, and a CliApp.serialize round-trip bug with CliUnknownArgs.

Security

  • SecretsSettingsSource no longer follows symlinks that resolve outside secrets_dir (#1138, fixes #1137). A secret file that is a symbolic link to a file outside secrets_dir was read into the matching field, so anyone who could place a link in secrets_dir could make the application load any file it can read. This is the plain-source counterpart of GHSA-4xgf-cpjx-pc3j, whose fix in 2.14.2 covered only NestedSecretsSettingsSource. Links that stay inside secrets_dir, such as the Kubernetes secret volume layout (passwd linking to ..data/passwd), still work.

Behavior changes

  • A secret file that resolves outside secrets_dir is now skipped with a warning instead of being read (#1138). If you deliberately point secret files at targets elsewhere on disk, move or copy the targets into secrets_dir, or point secrets_dir at the directory that holds them.
  • NestedSecretsSettingsSource skips hidden entries (names starting with .) again, as it did before 2.14.2, and stops with a SettingsError after 10,000 entries (#1070).

Bug fixes

Secrets

  • With secrets_nested_subdir=True, a directory reached through a second symlink is loaded again (#1070, fixes #1061). Since 2.14.2, only the name that sorted first was walked, so the standard Kubernetes secret volume layout (db linking to ..data/db) silently lost its nested secrets.
  • A symlink loop inside secrets_dir is skipped instead of aborting the load with RuntimeError on Python 3.11 and 3.12 (#1070, #1138).

CLI

  • CliApp.serialize keeps each level's CliUnknownArgs before that level's subcommand token (#1050, fixes #1048). They were emitted after the last subcommand, so parsing the output again moved a parent's unknown args onto the subcommand.

What's Changed

  • Fix CliApp.serialize moving a parent unknown args into the subcommand by @​XXXXXQ-0206 in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1050
  • Load nested secrets reached through a second directory link by @​digit50 in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1070
  • Prevent SecretsSettingsSource from following symlinks outside secrets_dir by @​twotnguyen in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1138

New Contributors

  • @​XXXXXQ-0206 made their first contribution in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1050
  • @​twotnguyen made their first contribution in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1138

Full Changelog: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-settings/compare/v2.16.2...v2.16.3

v2.16.2

Highlights

This patch release fixes env decoding of nested dictionary values, CliApp handling of AliasPath, nested secrets directory precedence and discriminated union defaults with nested_model_default_partial_update.

Behavior changes

  • An explicit secrets_dir on NestedSecretsSettingsSource now takes precedence (#1093). Previously it was ignored when the wrapped SecretsSettingsSource inherited a directory from model config, and an explicit empty list was masked too. The order is now: the wrapper's secrets_dir argument, then the wrapped source's directory, then model config. If you pass both Settings(_secrets_dir=...) and NestedSecretsSettingsSource(..., secrets_dir=...), the wrapper's argument now wins.

Updates `httpx2` from 2.16.0 to 2.16.2
Release notes

Sourced from httpx2's releases.

v2.16.2

🩹 Type aliases evaluate at runtime again

httpx2 and httpcore2 2.16.2 are a patch release with one fix. You will notice it if your code, or a library you depend on, uses the aliases in httpx2._types inside a runtime typing construct. On 2.16.1, import mistralai.client failed on Python 3.11 to 3.13.

pip install --upgrade httpx2==2.16.2
  • Optional[QueryParamTypes] and QueryParamTypes | None work again (#1346). In 2.16.1 URLTypes, QueryParamTypes, HeaderTypes, CookieTypes, TimeoutTypes, ProxyTypes and AuthTypes were strings. Optional[...] raised SyntaxError for QueryParamTypes and HeaderTypes, and | None raised TypeError for all seven. They are Union[...] objects again, as in 2.16.0.

httpcore2 has no changes. It is bumped to stay in lockstep with httpx2.

Full changelog: v2.16.1...v2.16.2

v2.16.1

🚦 Concurrent HTTP/2 uploads no longer stall

httpx2 and httpcore2 2.16.1 are a patch release. Every change is a fix. You will notice it most if you run several HTTP/2 uploads over one connection, where requests could hang until the read timeout.

pip install --upgrade httpx2==2.16.1
  • Uploads sharing an HTTP/2 connection finish instead of waiting for the read timeout (#1163). Once the flow control window was exhausted, a waiting upload could miss the WINDOW_UPDATE that another task had already read, then block on a read the server had nothing to answer. httpcore2 now rechecks the window after acquiring the read lock.
  • A missing Host header raises LocalProtocolError (#1319). An HTTP/2 request sent directly to an httpcore2 connection without Host raised IndexError before.

🧭 Redirects, proxies and Digest auth

  • A redirect with an invalid Location returns the response when redirects are not followed (#1064). httpx2 raised RemoteProtocolError and discarded the response. You now get the response with its headers, and response.next_request is None.
  • *.example.com in NO_PROXY matches subdomains (#1277). The entry never matched before, so those requests still went through the proxy. It now behaves like .example.com.
  • Digest challenges with mixed-case parameter names are accepted (#1315). A challenge such as Digest Realm="r", Nonce="n" raised ProtocolError before. Whitespace around = is allowed too.

📦 Signed releases

  • The publish workflow generates PEP 740 attestations (#1339). Every distribution is signed before uv publish uploads it. Releases since the move to uv publish had no provenance on PyPI.

Full changelog: v2.16.0...v2.16.1

Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.64.1 to 1.65.1
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.65.1

Bug Fixes

  • #43936 [Regression]: decorated class with a static field fails to load in 1.65 ("_initClass is not a function") with useDefineForClassFields: false
  • #43934 [Bug]: Test locations are one column off under Bun 1.4.4+

Browser Versions

  • Chromium 159.0.8154.6
  • Mozilla Firefox 159.0
  • WebKit 27.2

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 30.1.3 to 31.0.1.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v31.0.1

  • Improved performance of computed style reads, selector matching, CSS variable substitution, CSS shorthand updates, and focus handling on pages with many style rules. (@​scttcper)
  • Improved performance when building detached DOM trees and reading node.isConnected. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed element.tabIndex handling of invalid and out-of-range tabindex="" values to use the element's default instead of returning zero or wrapping. Values with trailing non-digits now use their leading integer, so tabindex="1e2" yields 1 instead of 100. (@​rome-xi)
  • Fixed CSS ident() results containing spaces or leading digits losing their required escaping during serialization and variable substitution. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed 'max-lines' values combining an integer and auto to serialize with the integer first, such as 3 auto.

v31.0.0

Breaking changes

  • Changed the optional canvas and image decoding backend from canvas to @napi-rs/canvas. Install @napi-rs/canvas v1.0.13 or later in the v1.x series alongside jsdom; installing canvas alone no longer enables this support. The new backend provides prebuilt Skia binaries on supported platforms, and rendering and encoded image bytes can differ. Projects using native canvas objects or custom font registration should follow the canvas migration guidance. Added WebP serialization through canvas.toDataURL() and canvas.toBlob(). Fixed image loading to wait for decoding before firing load, discard obsolete source requests, avoid refetching when dimensions change, and prevent failed images from drawing stale contents. Fixed canvas context and serialization behavior, including unsupported context types, read-only ctx.canvas, image-drawing exceptions, MIME type and quality normalization, and asynchronous null results from canvas.toBlob() for empty canvases or encoding failures. (@​Brooooooklyn)
  • Changed CSS parsing, selector matching, and computed styles to use a new integrated implementation, with substantially expanded support and faster selector queries and repeated style reads. This includes cascade layers, nesting, @scope, custom-property substitution and registration through @property and CSS.registerProperty(), typed attr(), conditional if(), shadow-tree styling with :host, ::slotted(), and ::part(), pseudo-element computed styles, and constructable stylesheets with document.adoptedStyleSheets and shadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets. Fixed numerous cascade, shorthand, serialization, and default-style issues; computed declarations now stay live across DOM and stylesheet changes. CSS serialization and computed values can differ from previous releases.
  • Changed HTML and XML parsing to pause at blocking scripts until their required resources are ready. The JSDOM constructor, JSDOM.fromURL(), and JSDOM.fromFile() can now return partially parsed documents. Wait for DOMContentLoaded for the finished tree, or the window's load event for load-delaying resources, checking document.readyState first in case the event has already fired. XML syntax errors encountered after asynchronous parsing resumes are reported through the virtual console as "xml-parsing" errors.

Other changes

  • Added window.reportError(), which dispatches an error event and reports uncanceled errors to the virtual console. (@​sarankumar1325)
  • Added element.ariaBrailleLabel and element.ariaBrailleRoleDescription. (@​Kjubikstronk)
  • Fixed page-completion load events to fire only on the window. Use window.addEventListener("load", ...) or window.onload instead of listening on the document.
  • Fixed document.open(), including implicit calls from document.write(), to clear event listeners and handlers from the document, its descendants, and its window when replacing the input stream.
  • Fixed document.write() to process successive writes through the parser's input stream, preserve insertion points across nested scripts, and make completed text immediately visible. Script-created input streams now remain open until document.close().
  • Fixed dynamically inserted scripts to respect script.async = false execution order, use their source text and document from preparation time, and avoid executing after adoption into another document. Scripts parsed through inert fragment APIs no longer execute when subsequently inserted.
  • Fixed unrelated images, stylesheets, and frames being delayed behind scripts, and resource completion events firing before nested stylesheet imports finish. Cyclic imports no longer prevent completion, and <style> elements in shadow trees now fire load events.
  • Fixed window.stop() to cancel pending subresource and XMLHttpRequest requests in descendant frames and suppress completion events for canceled loads, while allowing subsequent requests to proceed.
  • Fixed repeated document.close() calls replaying readiness and load events, and incorrect iframe load events when reopening documents from event handlers.
  • Fixed memory leaks where pending request interceptor promises retained closed windows, introduced in v28.0.0.
  • Fixed focus remaining on elements that become non-focusable after DOM or style changes. Focus now moves asynchronously to the document's viewport, and element.blur() can release it immediately.
  • Fixed document.hasFocus() returning false before an element is focused or during focus transitions within the document, including inside frames.
  • Fixed \<template> parsing and template.innerHTML serialization in XML documents, including templates with namespace prefixes. (@​b84330808)
  • Fixed rect.toJSON() and performance.toJSON() to create their result objects in the method's realm instead of the host Node.js realm.

  • 8a39b93 Track whether each node is connected
  • 463254b Speed up type and relative selector matching
  • afb7299 Fix max-lines serialization order
  • 574765e Fix tabIndex reflection of invalid and out-of-range values
  • 2cdcc44 Skip stylesheets that cannot apply to an element
  • 1ba3b6b Skip fetch cancellation test on affected Node versions
  • 40a0a14 Reduce CSS shorthand mutation overhead
  • 8a68119 Speed up CSS variable substitution
  • da2b11b Index pseudo-element rules apart from element rules

  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
  // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

  • test.skip(), test.fixme(), test.fail() and test.slow() now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

    test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
  test.skip('Not implemented yet');
});

Updates `jdx/mise-action` from 5.2.4 to 5.2.7
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/mise-action's releases.

v5.2.7: Retry failed mise downloads with backoff and show the HTTP status

When the action can't download mise, the log now shows the HTTP status and host for each failed attempt. Retries wait longer between attempts, so a short GitHub outage is less likely to fail the job.

Fixed

  • Download failures now show what went wrong, and brief outages are retried for longer. Before this release, a failed mise download logged only The process '/usr/bin/curl' failed with exit code 22 and retried five times with a fixed 2-second wait. From that message you couldn't tell a rate limit from a missing asset or a server error. Each failed attempt now logs the HTTP status and the host that answered:

    Download attempt 1/6 failed: Could not download github.com/…/mise-v2026.10.21-linux-x64.tar.zst (HTTP 503 from github.com). Retrying in 3.4 seconds.

    The wait between attempts doubles from about 2s up to a 30s cap, with random jitter, so the five retries cover roughly a minute. Only transient failures are retried: connection errors and timeouts, and HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx responses. A 404, any other 4xx, or a local file-write error fails at once. The log shows only the host and file name of each URL, never signed query strings or curl/wget stderr. Partial files are deleted before the next attempt. wget now runs with --tries=1, so its own 20-retry default no longer stacks on top of the action's retries. This applies to every download the action makes: the release archive, checksums and the packslip bundle. Checksum and signature verification are unchanged, and there are no new inputs. (#722 by @​jdx, fixes #721)

Changed

  • packslip, which the action uses to verify downloaded mise releases, is updated from 1.11.0 to 1.11.2. This version includes upstream hardening of its verifier checks. (#726)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.6...v5.2.7

v5.2.6: Fix step hanging after a failed cache restore

The action now exits as soon as its work is done. Before this release, a cache restore that failed during the download could leave the step running for up to ten minutes after setup had finished.

Fixed

  • A failed cache restore no longer leaves the step hanging. If the mise cache download failed partway through, for example with getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN, the action logged a warning, installed the tools and saved the cache, then stopped producing output. The step stayed in progress until the job was cancelled or a timer inside @actions/cacheactions/toolkit#2470Error objects now mark the step as failed with their message. Before, they caused an unhandled rejection. (#718 by @​jdx and @​kjanat, fixes #717)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.5...v5.2.6

v5.2.5: Bundled packslip verifier updated to 1.11.0; README examples use v5

This release updates the packslip library that the action uses to verify downloaded mise releases, and updates the README examples to use the current major versions.

Changed

  • packslip updated from 1.8.0 to 1.11.0. The action uses packslip to check a downloaded mise binary against the signed packslip.sigstore.json that ships with mise releases from 2026.9.3 onward. The new version runs extra checks on the signed statement: the identity it declares must match the certificate that signed it, and the certificate must belong to the github.com/jdx/mise repository. GitHub and GitLab repository names now match regardless of letter case. The action still asks for the same identity, issuer and tag as before, and there are no new inputs. (#715)
  • The README examples now use jdx/mise-action@v5 and actions/checkout@v7. (#710 by @​deining)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.4...v5.2.5

Updates `pydantic-settings` from 2.16.1 to 2.16.2
Release notes

Sourced from pydantic-settings's releases.

v2.16.2

Highlights

This patch release fixes env decoding of nested dictionary values, CliApp handling of AliasPath, nested secrets directory precedence and discriminated union defaults with nested_model_default_partial_update.

Behavior changes

  • An explicit secrets_dir on NestedSecretsSettingsSource now takes precedence (#1093). Previously it was ignored when the wrapped SecretsSettingsSource inherited a directory from model config, and an explicit empty list was masked too. The order is now: the wrapper's secrets_dir argument, then the wrapped source's directory, then model config. If you pass both Settings(_secrets_dir=...) and NestedSecretsSettingsSource(..., secrets_dir=...), the wrapper's argument now wins.

Bug fixes

Env and dotenv sources

  • Dictionary values typed as a union, such as dict[str, list[str] | str] or dict[str, list[str] | None], now JSON-decode values set through env_nested_delimiter (#1089, #1097). Only JSON arrays and objects are decoded, so plain values like 123, true or "quoted" are kept as strings. Decoding follows enable_decoding and the NoDecode/ForceDecode of the field that holds the dict, and type aliases and Annotated value types are resolved.
  • Nested dictionary values such as dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] are decoded at the right level again (#1109), so APP_VALUES__X='[{"k":"v"}]' no longer reaches validation as a string.

CLI

  • CliApp.run now rebuilds AliasPath inputs for BaseModel and pydantic dataclass commands (#1096). A supplied path used to be reduced to the field name, which failed validation. AliasChoices priority is respected and unsupplied path defaults are left to the model.

Discriminated union defaults

  • With nested_model_default_partial_update=True, inner discriminated unions written as Annotated[..., Field(discriminator='...')] are now detected (#1076). When the incoming tag selects another member, the default's fields are no longer merged into it.
  • A stdlib dataclass default on a discriminated union field no longer raises NameError when another field of the dataclass has a string annotation naming a local class (#1077). Only the discriminator's own annotation is resolved now.

What's Changed

  • build(deps): bump the python-packages group with 3 updates by @​dependabot[bot] in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1056

  • Decode nested dictionary values with complex union types by @​chering14 in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1089
  • Fix regressions from nested dict union value decoding (#1089) by @​hramezani in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1097
  • Fix explicit nested secrets directory precedence by @​DivyamTalwar in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1093
  • Fix CliApp reconstruction of AliasPath inputs by @​DivyamTalwar in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1096
  • Fix JSON decoding of nested dictionary environment values by @​Hugohong258 in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1109

Updates `sqlalchemy` from 2.1.6 to 2.1.8
Release notes

Sourced from sqlalchemy's releases.

2.1.8

Released: November 3, 2026

general

  • [general] [change] All files published to PyPI for a release, including the source distribution as well as all wheels, are now uploaded using PyPI's trusted publishing mechanism from SQLAlchemy's GitHub Actions workflow, and include a PEP 740 attestation, so that every file in a release carries provenance information. Previously, the source distribution and some wheels were uploaded without an attestation, which caused PyPI to display provenance warnings for recent releases.

    This change is also backported to: 2.0.57

    References: #13759

2.1.7

Released: November 3, 2026

orm

  • [orm] [feature] Added _orm.SessionTransaction.connections and _orm.SessionTransaction.bound_connection(), which return the connections a _orm.SessionTransaction has already acquired, without acquiring a new one. This allows, for example, checking whether any connection in the transaction has been invalidated before emitting further SQL. A SAVEPOINT transaction returned by _orm.Session.begin_nested() reports only the connections used within that SAVEPOINT; the root transaction returned by _orm.Session.get_transaction() reports all connections. The same accessors are available on _asyncio.AsyncSessionTransaction, returning _asyncio.AsyncConnection objects. Pull request courtesy Artur Shiriev.

    References: #13685

  • [orm] [bug] An informative InvalidRequestError is now raised when more than one PropComparator.of_type() loader option is applied along the same relationship using targets of differing classes, such as two _orm.aliased() constructs against different subclasses, which previously failed with a bare AssertionError during compilation. These options can't be combined since each target brings its own aliased copy of the base table; to load multiple subclasses along a single relationship, a single _orm.with_polymorphic() object that includes all of the target classes should be used.

Bumps the python-security group with 1 update in the / directory: [soupsieve](https://github.com/facelessuser/soupsieve). Updates `soupsieve` from 2.9.2 to 4.0
Release notes

Sourced from soupsieve's releases.

4.0

  • BREAK: The contents of an HTML template are no longer treated as part of the document. Selectors do not descend into a template, and elements inside one can't see beyond it, which also applies to pseudo-classes such as :lang(), :disabled, and :default. select and filter will still reach the contents of a template when they are called on the template itself, for example soup.template.select('p'). See the FAQ for more information.
  • BREAK: The contents of an iframe are no longer treated as a separate document, as they are not one in a browser. Elements in an iframe are normal children, so :root does not match them, and :default, :indeterminate, :checked, :dir(), :lang(), and :read-write treat them like any other element. Recent versions of html.parser, lxml, and html5lib all escape the contents of an iframe like a browser does, so this mostly affects XHTML, Python versions that still don't escape such content in their specific html.parser, and elements added to an iframe by hand. :-soup-contains() now also includes the escaped text in an iframe. See the FAQ for more information.
  • NEW: Update :disabled and :enabled to treat option and optgroup elements inside a disabled select as disabled, following a recent HTML specification update.
  • FIX: Fix the subsequent-sibling combinator and :has(~ ...) never matching top level elements of a fragment that has no root element, unless caching was disabled.
  • FIX: :indeterminate now treats a radio button group without a form as extending across the whole document instead of the top level element that contains it, and it no longer ignores radio buttons at the top level.
  • FIX: Fix :default to treat a button with a missing or invalid type, and an input with type="image", as submit buttons.
  • FIX: Fix :in-range and :out-of-range raising TypeError when the document contains an input without a type attribute.
  • FIX: :read-write (and :read-only) now treat contenteditable="plaintext-only" elements as editing hosts and match the editable elements inside an editing host, following the nearest contenteditable state.
  • FIX: :read-write (and :read-only) now ignore contenteditable on non-HTML elements, such as an SVG foreignObject, as the attribute only applies to HTML elements. Such elements inherit the state of their parent.
  • FIX: :checked now only matches the last radio button with a checked attribute in a radio button group, as in a browser, where a group is the radio buttons with the same name and form, including the form attribute. :default still matches all of them, and the contents of a template are unaffected as they are not connected.
  • FIX: :dir() and :defined no longer affect the rest of the selector list they are in. Previously, a selector list that used either of them could not have its combinators cross an iframe, ignored the specified namespaces, and matched nothing in XML, not even the parts that didn't use them. They still do not match in XML, but :not(:dir(ltr)) and :not(:defined) now do.
  • FIX: :default and :indeterminate now honor the form attribute, which can associate a submit button or radio button with a form it is not in, or leave it without a form. It is ignored in a template, as in the HTML specification. Submit buttons outside of a form can now be its default button.
  • FIX: :default, :checked, and :indeterminate now handle a form inside a form like a browser. In HTML, a browser ignores the nested form and takes its end tag for that of the parent, which matters for parsers that keep the nested form, such as html.parser. In XHTML and in a template, nested forms are real forms.
  • FIX: :checked now matches the option that a browser would select. Without multiple, that is only the last option with a selected attribute in a select, and if there are none and the select shows a single option, the first option that is not disabled. :default still only considers the selected attribute.
  • FIX: Fix [attribute!=value] excluding values that only start with the specified value, and in XML documents, type values that contain a newline.
  • FIX: Match the values of every attribute that the HTML specification lists as ASCII case insensitive (rel, method, lang, dir, ...) without ASCII case sensitivity on HTML elements in HTML documents, not just type. Non-HTML elements are matched case sensitively.

## Änderung

Ein leerer `Affected paths:`- oder `Betroffene Pfade:`-Abschnitt endet nun bei der ersten nachfolgenden Nicht-Listen-Zeile.
Eine spätere Markdown-Liste wird dadurch nicht mehr als Blockerpfad übernommen.
Regressionsfälle prüfen beide Überschriften und den geschlossenen PR-Check.

Closes #1219

## Prüfung

- `git diff --check`: erfolgreich.
- `python3 -m unittest tests.delivery.test_review_blockers -v`: 11 Tests erfolgreich.
- Projekt-Python 3.14.6 mit `PYTHONPATH=backend/src python3.14 -m unittest discover -s tests/delivery`: 76 Tests erfolgreich.
- Unabhängige C2-Code- und DevOps-Reviews auf `6fa99f9ddab058f26a8c23dca12544dafa794703`: keine bestätigten Befunde.

## Kontext und Grenzen

- Issue: https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/issues/1219.
- Complexity: C2 – Localized; Project: https://github.com/users/lxndrp/projects/2. Quelle: Maintainer-Kommentar https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/issues/1219#issuecomment-6572596914, erneut gelesen am 2026-11-09 08:10 UTC. Das Project-Feld war über die verfügbare API nicht direkt lesbar.
- PR-Head: `6fa99f9ddab058f26a8c23dca12544dafa794703`.
- Ausgewählte und geprüfte Perspektiven: lzug-code-review (C2) und lzug-devops-review (PR-Prozessautomation), jeweils unabhängig und read-only.
- `task test:delivery` konnte im isolierten Worktree wegen gesperrtem globalem uv-Cache und fehlendem Offline-Paket nicht starten; dieselbe 76 Tests umfassende Delivery-Discovery bestand mit dem projektgebundenen Python 3.14.6.
- [PR-CI 42584155073](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/42584155073) ist auf diesem Head rot: Downloads externer Task-, Python- und OpenTofu-Artefakte lieferten HTTP 504; abhängige Gates scheiterten dadurch ohne fachliche Testausführung. Backend-Qualität, Delivery-/Tooling-Verträge, Review-Blocker und CodeQL bestanden. Kein erneuter Workflowstart durch diesen Lauf.
- `task pr:create` konnte wegen fehlender `gh`-Anmeldung nicht starten; der Draft-PR wurde über die verbundene GitHub-Integration erstellt. Die PR-Project-Zuordnung konnte damit nicht gesetzt oder direkt geprüft werden; die Issue-Zuordnung ist dokumentiert.
- Ein Codex-GitHub-Review ist bisher nicht eingegangen. Der `pull_request_target`-Blockercheck liest bis zum Merge den Basisbranch-Code.

data.body:
## Ziel

Qualifiziert die vorhandene Produkt- und Demo-Containerisierung auf einem gehosteten Windows Server 2025 mit Microsoft wslc gegen den Runtime-Vertrag aus #941.

## Umfang

- Aktualisiert WSL über den offiziellen stabilen Update-Kanal und protokolliert Windows-/WSL-/wslc-Version, Architektur, CPU, Arbeitsspeicher und Buildzeiten.
- Baut die unveränderten Produkt- und Demo-Dockerfiles mit der Revision dieses PRs. Prüft kalte und wiederholte Builds, Plattform, Identität und Revision.
- Exportiert die gebauten Images als Archive und erzeugt daraus CycloneDX-SBOMs.
- Startet Produkt und Demo mit eindeutig benannten und markierten CI-Ressourcen. Prüft Readiness, Non-root, Loopback-Portbindung, Admin-Socket, synthetischen CLI-Schreib-/Leserundlauf sowie Datenpersistenz über Stop/Start.
- Prüft einen absichtlich fehlerhaften Dockerfile-Build auf einen Parserfehler ohne Wechsel auf Docker oder eine andere Engine.
- Entfernt ausschließlich Ressourcen dieses Workflow-Versuchs, deren Lauf-Label geprüft wurde. Der Build-Cache wird nicht global bereinigt.
- Bewahrt Diagnose, Laufzeitbefunde, Image-Archive und SBOMs sieben Tage als Workflow-Artefakte auf.
- Erzwingt LF für byte-gehashte SQL-Migrationen und vergleicht ihre Checkout-Bytes vor dem Build mit den Git-Blobs.
- Unterdrückt CLI-Antworten für den synthetischen Ausschuss-Bootstrap und dessen Replay, damit Einmal-Einladungstokens weder in Actions-Logs noch Fehlerausgaben gelangen.

## Aktueller Qualifikationsstand

Der vollständige gehostete Windows-Lauf [#9](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/42542141745) lief auf Windows Server 2025 mit WSL/wslc 3.0.3.0 (amd64, 4 vCPU, 16 GiB). GitHub führte den PR-Merge-Checkout `2bca471d` aus, der PR-Head `4f7aecd8` auf Basis `dd9c6bf5` enthält. Produkt-, Demo-Seed- und Demo-App-Images sowie ihre SBOMs wurden erstellt; kalte und gecachte Builds funktionierten. Produkt-Readiness, Health-Metadaten, Non-root, Loopback-Portbindung, Admin-Socket und synthetischer CLI-Schreib-/Leserundlauf nach Neustart bestanden. Demo-Initialisierung und Persistenz nach Neustart bestanden; alle laufbezogenen Container, Volumes und Images wurden bereinigt, der Cache blieb erhalten. Gemessene kalte/gecachte Builds: Produkt 159,26/4,13 s; Demo-Seed 29,20/1,86 s; Demo-App 131,34/2,76 s. Der Lauf endete erwartungsgemäß unvollständig: wslc bietet keine Read-only-Rootfs-, Capability-Drop- oder no-new-privileges-Option an und `container inspect` liefert kein `HostConfig.Privileged`; der Privilege-Modus bleibt deshalb ungeprüft. Die Evidence liegt als Workflow-Artefakt des Laufs vor. Die normale [Pull-Request-CI](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/42542141828) ist auf demselben Head grün. Die fehlenden Sicherheitsverträge bleiben konkrete externe Blocker, keine grünen Checks.

Die Qualifikation aktiviert noch keine allgemeine Engine-Auswahl und ändert keine Produktimages.

## Verifikation

- actionlint auf dem Qualifikationsworkflow
- PowerShell-Parserprüfung für `development/wslc/qualify.ps1`
- Ruff check/format für den Workflow-Vertragstest
- `tests.delivery.test_ci_workflow`: 30 Tests
- Lokaler Vergleich der SQL-Migrationsbytes mit den Git-Blobs
- Gehosteter Windows-Lauf für den aktuellen PR-Head: läuft

Tracks #941

Bumps the actions-routine group with 1 update: [jdx/mise-action](https://github.com/jdx/mise-action). Updates `jdx/mise-action` from 5.2.4 to 5.2.6
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/mise-action's releases.

v5.2.6: Fix step hanging after a failed cache restore

The action now exits as soon as its work is done. Before this release, a cache restore that failed during the download could leave the step running for up to ten minutes after setup had finished.

Fixed

  • A failed cache restore no longer leaves the step hanging. If the mise cache download failed partway through, for example with getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN, the action logged a warning, installed the tools and saved the cache, then stopped producing output. The step stayed in progress until the job was cancelled or a timer inside @actions/cacheactions/toolkit#2470Error objects now mark the step as failed with their message. Before, they caused an unhandled rejection. (#718 by @​jdx and @​kjanat, fixes #717)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.5...v5.2.6

v5.2.5: Bundled packslip verifier updated to 1.11.0; README examples use v5

This release updates the packslip library that the action uses to verify downloaded mise releases, and updates the README examples to use the current major versions.

Changed

  • packslip updated from 1.8.0 to 1.11.0. The action uses packslip to check a downloaded mise binary against the signed packslip.sigstore.json that ships with mise releases from 2026.9.3 onward. The new version runs extra checks on the signed statement: the identity it declares must match the certificate that signed it, and the certificate must belong to the github.com/jdx/mise repository. GitHub and GitLab repository names now match regardless of letter case. The action still asks for the same identity, issuer and tag as before, and there are no new inputs. (#715)
  • The README examples now use jdx/mise-action@v5 and actions/checkout@v7. (#710 by @​deining)

Updates `sass` from 1.106.1 to 1.107.1
Release notes

Sourced from sass's releases.

Dart Sass 1.107.1

To install Sass 1.107.1, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

  • Properly report the embedded protocol version as 3.4.0.

See the full changelog for changes in earlier releases.

Dart Sass 1.107.0

To install Sass 1.107.0, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

Command-Line Interface

  • The --fatal-deprecation flag can now exclude deprecations that would otherwise be included by passing a version number. To exclude a deprecation, add - before its name. For example, --fatal-deprecation=1.107.0,-import includes all deprecations that were present in Dart Sass 1.107.0 except for the @import deprecation.

  • The --fatal-deprecation flag now takes the special value dart-sass-2, which treats as fatal all deprecations that will become fatal in Dart Sass 2.0.0.

JavaScript API

  • Options.fatalDeprecations can now take a DeprecationSelectorDifference object of the form {include: ..., except: ...}, where the include field lists deprecations to mark fatal (which can be version numbers) and the except field lists deprecations not to mark fatal. The except field takes precedence over include.

  • Add a (non-enumerable) sass.deprecations.dartSass2 property which can be passed to Options.fatalDeprecations to mark as fatal exactly the deprecations that will become fatal in Dart Sass 2.0.0. This can be combined with other deprecations or used in a DeprecationSelectorDifference to modify exactly which deprecations it covers.

  • Passing a version number beyond the current Dart Sass version to Options.fatalDeprecations is now deprecated. See the Sass website for details.

Dart API

  • Add a Deprecation.dartSass2 property which returns exactly the set of deprecations that will become fatal in Dart Sass 2.0.0.

  • Passing a version number beyond the current Dart Sass version to Deprecation.forVersion is now deprecated.

Embedded Protocol

  • Add a CompileRequest.fatal_deprecation_except field which excludes deprecations from being considered fatal if they would have been enabled by CompileRequest.fatal_deprecation.

See the full changelog for changes in earlier releases.

Updates `pydantic-settings` from 2.16.1 to 2.16.2
Release notes

Sourced from pydantic-settings's releases.

v2.16.2

Highlights

This patch release fixes env decoding of nested dictionary values, CliApp handling of AliasPath, nested secrets directory precedence and discriminated union defaults with nested_model_default_partial_update.

Behavior changes

  • An explicit secrets_dir on NestedSecretsSettingsSource now takes precedence (#1093). Previously it was ignored when the wrapped SecretsSettingsSource inherited a directory from model config, and an explicit empty list was masked too. The order is now: the wrapper's secrets_dir argument, then the wrapped source's directory, then model config. If you pass both Settings(_secrets_dir=...) and NestedSecretsSettingsSource(..., secrets_dir=...), the wrapper's argument now wins.

Bug fixes

Env and dotenv sources

  • Dictionary values typed as a union, such as dict[str, list[str] | str] or dict[str, list[str] | None], now JSON-decode values set through env_nested_delimiter (#1089, #1097). Only JSON arrays and objects are decoded, so plain values like 123, true or "quoted" are kept as strings. Decoding follows enable_decoding and the NoDecode/ForceDecode of the field that holds the dict, and type aliases and Annotated value types are resolved.
  • Nested dictionary values such as dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] are decoded at the right level again (#1109), so APP_VALUES__X='[{"k":"v"}]' no longer reaches validation as a string.

CLI

  • CliApp.run now rebuilds AliasPath inputs for BaseModel and pydantic dataclass commands (#1096). A supplied path used to be reduced to the field name, which failed validation. AliasChoices priority is respected and unsupplied path defaults are left to the model.

Discriminated union defaults

  • With nested_model_default_partial_update=True, inner discriminated unions written as Annotated[..., Field(discriminator='...')] are now detected (#1076). When the incoming tag selects another member, the default's fields are no longer merged into it.
  • A stdlib dataclass default on a discriminated union field no longer raises NameError when another field of the dataclass has a string annotation naming a local class (#1077). Only the discriminator's own annotation is resolved now.

What's Changed

  • build(deps): bump the python-packages group with 3 updates by @​dependabot[bot] in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1056

  • Fix regressions from nested dict union value decoding (#1089) by @​hramezani in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1097
  • Fix explicit nested secrets directory precedence by @​DivyamTalwar in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1093
  • Fix CliApp reconstruction of AliasPath inputs by @​DivyamTalwar in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1096
  • Fix JSON decoding of nested dictionary environment values by @​Hugohong258 in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1109
  • Prepare release 2.16.2 by @​hramezani in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1111

Updates `sqlalchemy` from 2.1.6 to 2.1.8
Release notes

Sourced from sqlalchemy's releases.

2.1.8

Released: November 3, 2026

general

  • [general] [change] All files published to PyPI for a release, including the source distribution as well as all wheels, are now uploaded using PyPI's trusted publishing mechanism from SQLAlchemy's GitHub Actions workflow, and include a PEP 740 attestation, so that every file in a release carries provenance information. Previously, the source distribution and some wheels were uploaded without an attestation, which caused PyPI to display provenance warnings for recent releases.

    This change is also backported to: 2.0.57

    References: #13759

2.1.7

Released: November 3, 2026

orm

  • [orm] [feature] Added _orm.SessionTransaction.connections and _orm.SessionTransaction.bound_connection(), which return the connections a _orm.SessionTransaction has already acquired, without acquiring a new one. This allows, for example, checking whether any connection in the transaction has been invalidated before emitting further SQL. A SAVEPOINT transaction returned by _orm.Session.begin_nested() reports only the connections used within that SAVEPOINT; the root transaction returned by _orm.Session.get_transaction() reports all connections. The same accessors are available on _asyncio.AsyncSessionTransaction, returning _asyncio.AsyncConnection objects. Pull request courtesy Artur Shiriev.

    References: #13685

  • [orm] [bug] An informative InvalidRequestError is now raised when more than one PropComparator.of_type() loader option is applied along the same relationship using targets of differing classes, such as two _orm.aliased() constructs against different subclasses, which previously failed with a bare AssertionError during compilation. These options can't be combined since each target brings its own aliased copy of the base table; to load multiple subclasses along a single relationship, a single _orm.with_polymorphic() object that includes all of the target classes should be used.

data.body:
Bumps the codeql group with 2 updates in the / directory: [github/codeql-action/init](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) and [github/codeql-action/analyze](https://github.com/github/codeql-action). Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.39.1 to 4.39.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.4 - 20 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.5. #4333

4.39.3 - 04 Nov 2026

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

4.39.2 - 03 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. Updates `jdx/mise-action` from 5.2.2 to 5.2.4
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/mise-action's releases.

v5.2.4: Reuse cached signed checksums when restoring mise

Jobs that restore mise from the cache no longer have to download its signed checksums from GitHub on every run, so a network failure at that step no longer fails a job that otherwise restored correctly.

Fixed

  • Restoring a cached mise no longer needs a network download of the checksums. The action checks the cached mise binary against the signed SHASUMS256.txt and its .minisig. Before this release it downloaded both files from GitHub on every run, even when the cache restored correctly. When that download failed, for example after repeated curl errors, the job failed. Now, once the signature checks out, the action saves both files as SHASUMS256-<version>.txt and .minisig in <mise_dir>/bin, which is part of the mise cache. On later runs it reads them from the restored cache and checks the minisign signature again before using them. If the files are missing, corrupt or tampered with, the action downloads them as it did before. There are no new inputs. (#708 by @​jdx)
    • Caches saved by earlier versions don't contain these files. The main cache is only saved on a cache miss, so runs keep downloading the checksums until the cache is saved again or its key changes.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.3...v5.2.4

v5.2.3: Faster cache key computation in large workspaces

The cache key no longer comes from searching the whole workspace for mise config files. In repos that already contain node_modules or vendor/bundle, this removes a delay of several minutes in "Restoring mise cache".

Fixed

  • "Restoring mise cache" no longer takes minutes after installing dependencies. To build the cache key, the action used to match about 25 **/… glob patterns. That meant it walked every subdirectory of the workspace, including node_modules and vendor/bundle, before checking the cache at all. When the action ran after a step like pnpm install or ruby/setup-ruby with bundler-cache: true, this could take 3–7 minutes. The action now looks for mise config files the same way mise does: only in the working directory and each parent directory up to the workspace root. It checks for mise.toml, .mise.toml, .config/mise/…, conf.d fragments, .tool-versions, and their local, env-specific and .lock variants. The step also logs Hashed mise config files in N.Ns. (#703 by @​jdx and @​corsicanec82)
    • If you set a custom cache_key that doesn't use {{file_hash}} or {{default}}, the action no longer hashes config files at all.
    • Config files in subdirectories, such as monorepo sub-projects, no longer affect the cache key. mise only loads them with --monorepo.
    • Cache keys change, so the first run after you upgrade will miss the cache.

Bumps the python-routine group with 3 updates: [fastapi](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi), [sqlalchemy](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy) and [ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff). Updates `fastapi` from 0.156.8 to 0.162.0
Release notes

Sourced from fastapi's releases.

0.162.0

Omitted bool and bool | None form fields now use their declared defaults or produce missing-field errors, consistent with other fields and Pydantic behavior. FastAPI no longer infers False for omitted booleans. This applies to individual form parameters, form models, and unions of form models.

Omitted boolean model fields are excluded from model_dump(exclude_unset=True), and their defaults no longer count as submitted fields during union selection. Default factories and validate_default follow the usual rules.

For HTML checkboxes, declare a boolean with a default of False. See Boolean Form Fields.

Breaking Changes

  • 🐛 Restore default handling for omitted boolean form fields. PR #16605 by @​tiangolo.

0.161.1

Fixes

  • 🐛 Fix OpenAPI schemas for standalone nullable form unions. PR #16598 by @​tiangolo.

0.161.0

Features

  • ✨ Add support for combining unions of form models. PR #16596 by @​tiangolo.

0.160.0

Query, header, cookie, and form parameter models now apply their extra configuration to all submitted fields in the same parameter location, consistent with Pydantic behavior. This includes fields declared in other models, individual parameters, or dependencies, which were previously excluded.

With extra="forbid", fields outside the model are rejected even if another parameter declares them. With extra="allow", those fields are included as model extras. With the default extra="ignore", they are ignored.

Breaking Changes

  • 🐛 Apply each parameter model's extra configuration to sibling fields. PR #16594 by @​tiangolo.

Internal

  • ⬆ Bump certifi from 2026.1.4 to 2026.10.19. PR #16571 by @​dependabot[bot].

0.159.1

Features

  • ✨ Add support for optional unions of form models. PR #16586 by @​tiangolo.

0.159.0

Features

  • ✨ Add support for optional query, header, and cookie parameter models. PR #16584 by @​tiangolo.

Updates `sqlalchemy` from 2.1.5 to 2.1.6
Release notes

Sourced from sqlalchemy's releases.

2.1.6

Released: October 21, 2026

orm

  • [orm] [bug] Fixed issue where a Session flush that replaced an expired object in the identity map with a newly flushed object of the same primary key would emit a SELECT to refresh the expired object, solely in order to determine whether to emit an "Identity map already had an identity" warning. This could occur when a row loaded within a transaction is rolled back and its primary key value is subsequently reused, and could lead to an AttributeError if the expired object were garbage collected during that load. The check now emits no SQL, and an expired object that is replaced in this way no longer causes the warning to be emitted.

    This change is also backported to: 2.0.56

    References: #13711

  • [orm] [bug] [regression] Fixed regression caused by #13070 where using more than one orm.with_loader_criteria() option for the same entity, where the criteria made use of correlated subqueries referring to that entity, would fail with a RecursionError when compiling.

    References: #13701

  • [orm] [bug] [regression] Fixed regression caused by the new implementation of .params() for statements introduced in #7066, where parameter values passed to the .params() method of an ORM statement created using Select.from_statement() would not be applied when the statement was compiled without the compiled statement cache, such as when the cache was disabled or when the statement was stringified directly, leading to an error that a value is required for the bound parameter.

    References: #13709

orm extensions

  • [bug] [orm extensions] Fixed an issue in the instrumentation_toplevel extension where unrelated classes inheriting from typing.Generic could incorrectly raise a TypeError when using different instrumentation implementations. Pull request courtesy TomasCaruso10.

    This change is also backported to: 2.0.56

    References: #13680

data.body:
Closes #1202

## Summary

- Add a read-only GitHub Actions check that blocks changed paths overlapping open issues labeled `review:blocking`.
- Skip blockers explicitly closed by this PR; preserve other matching blockers.
- Fail closed when GitHub data, issue paths, renamed paths, or the complete PR file list cannot be read or parsed.
- Document the stable check name `Review blockers / Review blockers`, Required Check setup, human-only label meaning, and rerun requirements.

## Verification

- Focused blocker and workflow contract tests: 37 passed.
- Ruff, actionlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent C2 code and DevOps reviews of base `ca8715f8` and head `fbf5ee00`: no confirmed findings.
- GitHub Pull Request run #1452 and Public site run #1649 passed for head `fbf5ee00`.
- The local full `task quality` attempt was limited by blocked Docker, network, and socket access; all PR CI jobs passed.

## Maintainer follow-up

The repository label `review:blocking` is not present yet. The connected GitHub API exposes no label-creation operation, and local `gh` authentication is invalid, so it could not be provisioned from this task. Required-check activation remains a separate maintainer action. The new workflow cannot run on its introducing PR until the workflow exists on the base branch.

data.body:
## Ziel

- Den bestehenden lokalen Codebasis-Review nach bestätigten Befunden automatisch in die reguläre Issue-Reifeprüfung und gegebenenfalls Issue-Delivery überführen.
- Reife-, Blocker-, Wiederholungs- und Draft-PR-Grenzen in den Projektregeln dokumentieren.
- Den bestehenden Wochenlauf beibehalten; keine automatische Priorisierung, Planänderung oder Mergefreigabe einführen.

## Nachweis

- [x] Neu bestätigte Befunde werden ohne zusätzliches `review:auto-fix`-Label auf Reife geprüft; offene, zuvor blockierte Befunde können nach geklärten Blockern erneut geprüft werden.
- [x] Unreife Befunde bleiben offen und erhalten den konkreten fehlenden Planungsinhalt; Reifeprüfung verlangt vollständige Kriterien, keine `needs:*`-Blocker, keine konkurrierende Umsetzung und belegte Complexity.
- [x] Reife Befunde bearbeiten einen eigenen Issue-Worktree; vorhandene Arbeit wird berücksichtigt. Erfolgreiche Umsetzung erzeugt einen Draft-PR mit `Closes #1201`; kein Auto-Merge oder Planwert-Update.
- [x] Bestehender lokaler Wochenlauf auf automatische Reifeprüfung und Delivery aktualisiert; Zeitplan, lokales Umfeld, Modell und Projektzuordnung unverändert.
- [x] `git diff --check` bestanden.
- [x] `task docs`: 11 Dokumentationstests, Media- und CLI-Prüfung bestanden.
- [ ] Vollständiger MkDocs-Build lokal nicht abgeschlossen: der strikte URL-Check konnte `https://unpkg.com/mermaid@10.4.0/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs` wegen fehlendem Netzzugriff nicht abrufen.
- [x] GitHub Actions auf Head `8142d3b33e22da0b645427be4808bc67d825d111`: Pull Request run #1448 und Public site run #1644 erfolgreich.
- [x] Unabhängiger Code-Review (C2) und DevOps-Review auf Base `32d64e0f2b842c9daa8df67312817a2ef7a8e106` / Head `8142d3b33e22da0b645427be4808bc67d825d111`; keine bestätigten Befunde.
- [x] Codex Code- und Security-Review auf diesem Head abgeschlossen; keine Befunde oder offenen Review-Threads.

### Reviewkontext

- Auftragsissue: #1201; Complexity: C2 - Localized.
- Project-Quelle: https://github.com/users/lxndrp/projects/2; live gelesen am 2026-10-27 16:34 UTC, für diesen Scope und Head übergeben.
- Geprüfte Perspektiven: lzug-code-review und lzug-devops-review; beide unabhängig auf Base/Head oben, ohne Befunde.
- PR-CI: https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/40544464556
- Public site: https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/40544463746
- Lokaler MkDocs-Build bleibt wegen der Netzgrenze offen; die GitHub-Dokumentationsprüfung und beide Actions-Runs waren erfolgreich.

## Abweichungen

Der bestehende lokale Wochenlauf wurde nach ausdrücklicher Nutzerfreigabe aktualisiert. Sein bestehender Zeitplan und seine übrigen Einstellungen bleiben unverändert. Diese persönliche Codex-Konfiguration liegt außerhalb des versionierten Diffs.

## Verknüpfung

Closes #1201

data.body:
This is the local Ubuntu 24.04 quality-runner pilot for #1005. `mise exec -- task quality:ubuntu` invokes the existing project-wide `task quality` suite inside Ubuntu; Task remains the sole suite definition. The runner uses the local Docker Engine socket, derives Playwright from the frontend lockfile, keeps Linux dependencies and caches separate from host artifacts, and preserves the worktree path for nested Docker bind mounts.

The runner keeps Chromium's sandbox enabled with the Playwright-matched seccomp profile. Worktree-scoped labels and name prefixes cover runner images, volumes, Buildx state, Pester fixture resources, and demo smoke resources so the Codex Environment cleanup can identify them. One-shot Pester CLI containers use `--rm`; the runner validates Docker's local socket endpoint and only removes stale runner containers when both generated name and label match.

## Verification

- `mise exec -- task quality:ubuntu` completed twice with exit code 0 on the Mac mini, using Docker's `linux/arm64` runner allocation (4 vCPUs, about 3.82 GiB RAM). Both runs began with empty package/build caches and completed in about 10–11 minutes.
- The first run had no Playwright retries. In the second, four browser tests passed on retry; backend coverage, 17 Pester tests, demo smoke, infrastructure checks, and the remaining browser tests passed. `task docs` also passed after the documentation adjustment.
- Linux/AMD64 reference: [Quality run #40379412799](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/40379412799) on `dc4df1ba`, 64m39s total. This is contextual evidence, not a direct benchmark, because CI splits work into parallel jobs and uses different caches.
- Decision: do not reuse the local runner image in GitHub Actions. Existing CI jobs already run the same Task contracts in purpose-specific Ubuntu jobs; the local image would not replace their job boundaries or OS matrix and adds no measured maintenance benefit.
- Cleanup was verified: BuildKit cache is 0 B; runner containers, test volumes, and temporary directories were removed. The approximately 943 MB BuildKit base image and two pre-existing Pester containers/volumes were preserved.
- Final implementation head: `23881c78074e5a3b7cc8bf6166db70206780e622`. `mise exec -- task quality:ubuntu` completed with exit code 0; the runner was built with host UID 501 and kept non-root. The Pester runner contracts passed 18/18.
- A full native Mac mini M6 `task quality` completed with exit code 0 using the project-managed Node and Playwright versions. The run set `CI=true` and used a temporary Playwright browser path; it ran outside Codex's macOS sandbox because Chromium's Mach-port bootstrap is denied inside that sandbox.
- On this head, Pull Request workflow [#42545276894](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/42545276894) passed. Public Site workflow [#42545276927](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/42545276927) failed only at the external linkcheck after one timeout to the configured demo URL; browser and accessibility steps passed.
- Independent C3 Code, Application Architecture, and DevOps reviews found no confirmed findings on the UID follow-up; the P2 review thread is resolved.

The implementation for #1005 is complete. The external Public Site linkcheck remains to be rerun after its demo-origin timeout; merge still requires maintainer authorization.

## Summary

Define the local OCI runtime contract in ADR-0043 while retaining ADR-0033 as the accepted production-runtime decision. Local qualification is tied to the host OS/version, architecture, engine and engine version; that requirement also applies to Docker when used as a local fallback. The Linux CI/release reference does not imply qualification on other hosts. The contract also binds SBOM and runtime evidence to the same product, demo-app and seed image artifacts and defines scoped resource cleanup.

The contract test protects platform selection, fail-closed fallback, Docker host qualification, per-image evidence and cleanup rules. #942 must enumerate each offered host/runtime tuple and its qualification evidence. Real Apple Container, Podman and wslc qualification remains in #939–#941.

## Ziel

Der im Quality-Lauf geprüfte Produktcontainer meldete CVEs. Dieser PR hebt den Go-Toolchain-Pin auf 1.26.10, wechselt die Python-Stufen des Produktimages auf Debian Trixie und aktualisiert die Runtime-Pakete beim Image-Build. Mindestversionen für die zuvor betroffenen OpenSSL- und Perl-Pakete werden geprüft.

data.body:
## Summary

Closes #1154.

Collect machine-readable per-test and per-module duration reports, then balance HTTP test shards from measured module runtimes. Modules without measurements use a deterministic test-count estimate, keeping first-run and newly added modules covered. CI publishes the reports as artifacts, and the local workflow is documented.

Linux profiling confirmed that repeated fixture/database preparation was not a dominant cost, so the tests retain per-execution database isolation and no shared mutable fixture state was introduced. Test tiers, test count, order independence, coverage, and PR gates remain intact.

## Linux evidence

- Existing Ubuntu 24.04 PR quality baseline: 108 s on `308884b` (from #1154 evidence).
- Existing unsharded Linux baseline: 810 tests in 115.9 s on `a3b4537`, with 17 slow-test warnings (from #1154 evidence).
- Final GitHub Actions backend run `40300250994` used `ubuntu-24.04` / Python 3.14.6 x64. Reports bind merge checkout `95a66dd` to PR head `ed287d7` and cover 814 tests across all tiers (69 unit, 317 component, 70 process, 358 HTTP).
- Final HTTP shard measurements were 175.99 s, 178.82 s, and 175.08 s. All four test tiers passed on the final head. A prior run exposed a test that inherited the CI PR-head environment; follow-up commit `ed287d7` isolated that test and passed on CI.
- A local Linux Docker Desktop arm64 full run passed 814 tests with 3 optional skips in 111.653 s; a full coverage run passed 814 tests with 3 optional skips in 117.196 s (88% total coverage).

## Validation

The focused `backend.tests.test_tiers` suite passes (10 tests) after the environment-isolation fix. Mypy, repository-wide Ruff, Black check, actionlint, and `git diff --check` passed on the implementation.

The Python dependency audit remains red because the unchanged lockfile has 14 existing advisories across five packages (including `aiohttp` 3.14.3, fixed upstream in 3.14.4). I checked open issues for Python dependency vulnerabilities, `pip audit`, and aiohttp; no matching open issue was found. This unrelated dependency work is outside #1154.

data.body:
## Ziel

Die Frontend-Architekturprüfung verwendet generische Modul- und Abhängigkeitsgrenzen statt fest verdrahteter Klassenlisten und Orts-/Dashboard-Topologieannahmen. Der Check verfolgt statische und dynamische Imports sowie Re-Exports, prüft API-, HTTP-, Transport-, Adapter-, Port- und Composition-Root-Grenzen und verlangt keine vorgeschriebenen Helper-Namen oder Weiterleitungsketten.

Der frühere Orts-Sondercheck wurde entfernt. Architekturfixtures decken erlaubte und verbotene Abhängigkeiten, verschachtelte Barrels, dynamische Imports, Import-Type-Ausdrücke, direkte `fetch()`-Aufrufe, Portbindungen und beliebig benannte transitive Helper ab. Die Komponenten-, Entwicklungs- und Frontend-Architekturdokumentation beschreibt die neuen Grenzen und verweist auf Laufzeitregressionen für unabhängige Orts-Reads, Session-/Kontextbindung, fortlebende Mutationen sowie Export- und Fehlerverträge. Laufzeit- und Backendverträge wurden nicht geändert; Diagramme, Pages und Wiki sind nicht betroffen.

Closes #1103

## Prüfung

- Finaler Head: `4134fb49e8786582ee5f011c3c155a4761bcf822`.
- `npm run architecture:check`: 21 Fixtures und vollständiger Frontend-Repository-Scan bestanden; der finale CI-Job `Frontend details` hat den Check explizit ausgeführt.
- Frontend-CI: 61 Testdateien, 491 Tests bestanden. Darin enthalten sind die dokumentierten Regressionen in `locations-workspace.facade.spec.ts`, `planning-workflow.service.spec.ts`, `session-scope.service.spec.ts`, `exam-day.facade.spec.ts` und den HTTP-Adaptertests für Halbjahre, Protokoll und Ergebnis.
- Finale PR-CI: Backend, CLI, Container, Dokumentation, OpenAPI-Generierung, CodeQL, Secret-/Misconfiguration-Scan, Workflow-Syntax und statischer Artefakt-Build bestanden. Nicht betroffene optionale Jobs wurden übersprungen.
- CodeQL: keine neuen Alerts im PR-Code. Die Sprachjobs melden zusätzlich eine bestehende Workflow-Konfigurationswarnung zu fehlenden `on.push`-Hooks für Default-Branch-Scans.
- `git diff --check` bestanden.
- Ein früherer breiter lokaler `mise exec -- task quality`-Lauf war nicht vollständig grün: Security-Audit-Advisories bereits gesperrter Abhängigkeiten sowie zwei unabhängige E2E-Fehler in Master-Data- und Planning-Synchronisationsprüfungen. Diese Bereiche sind nicht Teil des Diffs. Die finale CI am oben genannten Head ist grün.

## Review

Complexity für #1103 wurde am 2026-10-26 um 08:44 UTC live aus Project #2 als C3 – Crosscutting gelesen; Priority P1 – High, Status In Progress. Project: https://github.com/users/lxndrp/projects/2.

- Unabhängiger C3-Code-Review des vollständigen 14-Dateien-Diffs von Base `de9c931e9c3224389d4a1ddac6a0246020cbd127` bis Head `4134fb49e8786582ee5f011c3c155a4761bcf822`: keine bestätigten Befunde.
- Unabhängiger C3-Anwendungsarchitektur-Review desselben vollständigen Diffs: keine bestätigten Befunde.
- Prüflücke: Die Exportauflösung deckt `export { X } from './module'` und `export *` ab, aber nicht das lokale Muster `import { X } from './module'; export { X };`. Die vollständige Anwendungsarchitekturprüfung fand kein solches Muster im aktuellen Composition Root; daher kein bestätigter Befund für diesen Diff.
- Der GitHub-Codex-Code-Review bezieht sich noch auf den älteren Head `9c8388f`. Sein P2 zu API-Client-Imports in Facades/Workflows ist behoben; der Thread ist aufgelöst und veraltet. Der parallel gemeldete GitHub-Codex-Security-Review läuft weiterhin nur für diesen alten Head und ist kein Sicherheitsnachweis für den aktuellen Stand. Für `4134fb4` wurde kein neuer öffentlicher Codex-Review-Kommentar ausgelöst.

## Summary

- Use generated OpenAPI request and response contracts at frontend adapter boundaries, then map them into feature-owned models.
- Remove duplicate full transport models, the generic link-stripping helper, and result camelizing/assertion logic.
- Keep narrow typed projections where OpenAPI responses remain unknown; explicitly validate open fields and narrow feature enums.
- Preserve nullable and optional behavior such as `day_revision`, project Confirm warnings and nested HAL links, and keep Dashboard ports on feature-owned models.
- The eight-file follow-up in commit `2ba4181572811ec0468f0d47f71378392db8c165` removes nested HAL links from the planning and dashboard projections and gives Dashboard its own read models.

## Validation

- App and spec TypeScript checks — passed.
- Frontend architecture checks and Prettier on changed files — passed.
- Documented Angular test entry point — passed; 57 test files and 466 tests.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Pull Request CI run [40220267040](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/40220267040) for head `2ba4181572811ec0468f0d47f71378392db8c165` — passed.

## Änderungen

- Die sieben einzelnen Abschluss-/Wiederöffnungsfelder sind in zwei typisierte Angular-Formulargruppen mit gruppenweiter Validierung überführt.
- Formularwerte werden explizit auf die bestehenden Commands abgebildet; regulärer Abschluss bleibt ohne Ausnahmefelder möglich.
- Tages- und Session-Kontextwechsel setzen beide Entwürfe zurück; Refreshes desselben Tages erhalten sie.
- Der Wiederöffnungsscope wird zur Laufzeit geprüft statt ungeprüft gecastet.
- `docs/developers/components.md` beschreibt nun die typisierten FormGroups und deren Validierungs-/Command-Vertrag.

## Erhaltenes Verhalten und lokale Prüfung

- Leerraum-only Ausnahmeangaben verhindern den Abschluss-Command.
- Der Browserpfad prüft Tastaturfokus, mobile Darstellung, Axe-Verstöße und das Command-Payload-Mapping.
- Am Code-Head `b417f013248f0444c03e053ae23820b003ce868f` bestanden: `npm run test:ci` (57 Dateien, 454 Tests), `npm run build:ci`, gezielter Chromium-/Axe-Test, Prettier, ESLint und `git diff --check`.
- Die Dokuergänzung am damaligen Head `45a74982cb31ef78988341535a5d43005754ca34` ist geprüft; `git diff --check` passt. Prettier würde vorhandene Tabellen im Dokument umbrechen, ändert aber den ergänzten Absatz nicht.
- Build-generierte, sachfremde Änderungen an `types.gen.ts` wurden verworfen.

## CI, Reviews und Follow-up

- PR-CI auf Head `03f1db975d344d826639aa4f0fad30ea1cf68891`: erfolgreich ([Run](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/40236023459)).
- Der dokumentierte Public-Site-Lauf auf dem vorherigen Head wurde abgebrochen ([Run](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/40217232439)); zuvor scheiterte der Linkcheck an externen GitHub-Blob-URLs mit HTTP 503. Auf dem aktuellen Head wurde dafür kein neuer Lauf gestartet.
- Der GitHub-Code-Review auf dem aktuellen Head fand einen P2: Nach Wechsel von Ausnahmeabschluss mit leeren Feldern zurück zu „Regulär“ können bedingte `required`-Validatoren den regulären Abschluss weiterhin blockieren.
- Der Security-Review auf dem aktuellen Head ist ohne Befund. Unabhängige lokale Code-, Anwendungs- und Systemarchitektur-Reviews fanden keine weiteren Befunde; der Code-Review übersah den genannten Übergangspfad.
- #1102 wurde für die gezielte Korrektur wieder geöffnet. Der Follow-up verlangt gruppenbasierte Pflichtvalidierung, erhaltene zugängliche Required-Semantik und einen Regressionstest für Ausnahme → regulär mit leeren Feldern.

## Dokumentationsentscheidung

Architekturdiagramme bleiben unverändert, weil Modulgrenzen und Draft-Lebensdauer gleich bleiben. Pages und Wiki sind nicht betroffen, da sich keine Bedien- oder Betriebsverträge ändern.

## Änderung

- Protokoll und Ergebnis verwenden einen gemeinsamen discriminated `LoadState<T>` mit `loading`/`error` samt ausdrücklich erhaltenen vorherigen Daten, `ready` und kontextgeschütztem `not-found`.

- Es gibt keine gemeinsame Request-Engine: Latest-Read, Duplikatunterdrückung und serialisierte Commands haben unterschiedliche Policies. Die Architekturgrenze und diese bewusste Resttrennung sind dokumentiert.

Bumps the frontend-security group with 2 updates in the /frontend directory: [fast-uri](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri) and [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici). Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

What's Changed

  • ci: enable trusted publishing releases (v3.x) by @​mcollina in fastify/fast-uri#229
