Updates `undici` from 8.11.2 to 8.12.3
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v8.12.3

What's Changed

  • ci: use Python 3.14 for the WPT server on macOS by @​mrityunjay-pandey in nodejs/undici#6029
  • build(deps-dev): bump neostandard from 0.13.0 to 0.14.0 by @​dependabot[bot] in nodejs/undici#6006
  • build(deps-dev): bump eslint from 9.39.4 to 10.12.0 by @​dependabot[bot] in nodejs/undici#5967

  • fix(h2): replace a connection that stops responding after a stream timeout by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6052
  • fix(pool): keep caller async context for queued requests by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#5982

New Contributors

  • @​qodelicious made their first contribution in nodejs/undici#6050

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v8.12.2...v8.12.3

v8.12.2

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

Updates `jdx/mise-action` from 5.0.1 to 5.2.2
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/mise-action's releases.

v5.2.2: Include conf.d config fragments in the cache key

The cache key now includes mise conf.d/*.toml config fragments, so changing one of them invalidates the cache.

Fixed

  • Editing a conf.d fragment now invalidates the cache. mise can load config from single-file fragments in conf.d/ directories, but the action didn't hash those files when it built the cache key. As a result, adding or changing tools in a fragment could restore an outdated cache. The cache key now also hashes conf.d/*.toml files under .config/mise/, .mise/ and mise/. If your repo already uses these fragments, the cache will miss once after you upgrade. (#698 by @​rileymichael)

New Contributors

  • @​rileymichael made their first contribution in #698

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.1...v5.2.2

v5.2.1: Require the signed packslip for mise 2026.9.3 and later

The action now refuses to install mise 2026.9.3 or later if the release's signed packslip is missing. This closes a gap where verification could be downgraded to the weaker checksum check.

Fixed

  • A missing packslip no longer weakens the check on recent mise releases. v5.2.0 started checking the mise binary against the release's signed packslip.sigstore.json. If that file wasn't found, though, the action quietly fell back to the minisign-signed SHASUMS256 checksums. Anyone who could hide the file could force the weaker check. Every mise release from 2026.9.3 on includes a packslip, so for those versions a missing bundle now stops the install with an error like this: 
    mise v2026.10.11 must ship a signed packslip, but https://github.com/jdx/mise/releases/download/v2026.10.11/packslip.sigstore.json was not found
    Releases before 2026.9.3 don't include a packslip, so they're still checked against the signed checksums. A version string that isn't three dot-separated numbers also requires a packslip. If you set the sha256 input, it still takes precedence over both checks. A packslip that fails verification still never falls back to the checksums. (#695 by @​jdx)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.0...v5.2.1

v5.2.0: Periodic cache rebuilds, signed packslip verification, and monorepo installs

The default cache key now rolls over every 30 days, so long-lived caches pick up newer mise releases. The action also checks the downloaded mise binary against the release's signed packslip, and it runs mise install --monorepo automatically in monorepos. Existing caches miss once after you upgrade, because the default cache key format has changed.

Added

  • The cache is rebuilt every 30 days by default. GitHub never evicts a cache that keeps getting hits. Before this release, an active repo could keep the same mise binary and tools for months, until a config file changed. The default cache key now includes a period suffix (-p<N>), so the cache is rebuilt from scratch at least once per period. All repos roll over on the same calendar boundary. Use the new cache_max_age_days input to change the period, or set it to 0 to keep the old key that never expires. Custom cache_key templates can use the new {{cache_period}} variable, which {{default}} already includes. A custom key that doesn't use it behaves as before. On self-hosted runners that keep mise data between runs, you may also need auto_update: true to pick up a newer mise. (#689 by @​jdx, fixes #688) 
    - uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
  with:
    cache_max_age_days: 14 # default 30; 0 disables periodic rebuilds
  • Throttled cache restores and saves can be retried. Before this release, when GitHub's cache service returned HTTP 429, the action gave up right away: a restore counted as a miss and a save was skipped. The new cache_restore_retry_budget and cache_save_retry_budget inputs set how long the action may wait. Each retry waits for the Retry-After value plus some random jitter. Once the budget runs out, the action falls back to the old behavior. Retries apply to the main cache, the post-step save and the binary cache. Real cache misses and reservation conflicts are never retried. Both budgets default to 0s (no retries). @actions/cache doesn't report 429 errors directly, so the action detects throttling from its warning messages. If those messages change in a future @actions/cache release, throttling won't be detected and nothing will be retried. (#692 by @​jdx, fixes #691) 
    - uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
  with:
    cache_restore_retry_budget: 60s
    cache_save_retry_budget: 120s
  • The latest mise binary can fall back to a second download source. When the action downloads the latest mise version, it can fall back between GitHub and mise.jdx.dev if the first source fails. The fetch_from_github setting decides which source it tries first. Pinned versions and minimum_release_age installs are only downloaded from GitHub. The binary is still checked against the signed checksums for the resolved version, whichever source it came from. (#692 by @​jdx)
  • The mise binary is checked against its signed packslip. If a mise release includes packslip.sigstore.json, the action checks the downloaded binary against it. The bundle must be signed by mise's release workflow for that exact tag. After a successful check, the log shows Verified <asset> against the signed packslip. If the check fails, the install stops instead of falling back to a weaker check. Releases without a packslip use the existing minisign and SHASUMS256 check. An explicit sha256 input still takes precedence. (#693 by @​jdx)
  • Monorepo-aware installs. If your mise config sets [monorepo].config_roots, the action now adds --monorepo to mise install, so tools configured anywhere in the monorepo get installed. Repos without that setting aren't affected. To opt out, set monorepo: false. (#679 by @​zeitlinger)

Fixed

Updates `pydantic-settings` from 2.16.0 to 2.16.1
Release notes

Sourced from pydantic-settings's releases.

v2.16.1

Highlights

This patch release fixes two CLI regressions introduced in 2.16.0.

Bug fixes

CLI

  • Fixed-length tuple positionals such as CliPositionalArg[tuple[int, int]] and NamedTuples are single-valued again (#1069). Since 2.16.0 they were treated as variadic, so a CLI either refused to start with a SettingsError or put the wrong argument into the tuple. Variable-length tuples (tuple[int, ...] and bare Tuple) are still variadic.
  • A field typed as an alias of a list of dicts, e.g. type ListOfDict = list[dict[str, int]], accepts a JSON list again (#1049). Since 2.16.0, --xx '[{"a":1},{"b":2}]' was merged into the single dict {"a": 1, "b": 2} and failed validation.

What's Changed

  • Harden CI by @​Viicos in pydantic/pydantic-settings#1044

Updates `httpx2` from 2.13.1 to 2.16.0
Release notes

Sourced from httpx2's releases.

v2.16.0

Highlights

🍪 Faster requests with large cookie jars

Building the Cookie header no longer scans every cookie in the jar. The client reuses its jar instead of copying it on every request and redirect (#1284), only looks up the domains that can match the request host, and skips the expired cookie sweep until a cookie is due (#1285). With 1,000 cookies across 500 domains, building the Cookie header is about 18 times faster.

Cookies from different domains are now sent from the least to the most specific domain, for example .example.org before sub.example.org, instead of in the order the domains were added. Cookies with longer paths still come first.

httpx2

Changed

  • Look up only the cookie domains that match the request host, and skip the expired cookie sweep until a cookie is due. With 1,000 cookies across 500 domains, building the Cookie header is about 18 times faster. Cookies from different domains are now sent from the least to the most specific domain (#1285).

Fixed

  • Reuse the client cookie jar instead of copying it on every request and redirect. A custom policy set with client.cookies.jar.set_policy() now applies to outgoing requests (#1284).

httpcore2

No changes since 2.15.1. Version bumped to stay in lockstep with httpx2.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/pydantic/httpx2/compare/v2.15.1...v2.16.0

v2.15.1

Highlights

🔒 Flat CPU usage for long-lived clients on Linux

On Linux, the default SSL context is now configured once instead of on every handshake (#1253). With OpenSSL older than 3.4, each handshake added a duplicate certificate lookup path, so CPU usage per request grew over the lifetime of a reused client. Certificate verification is unchanged, and Windows and macOS still use truststore.

  • Improved performance of getComputedStyle() and computed CSS property reads, including with stylesheets containing attribute selectors. (@​scttcper, @​asamuzaK)

  • Fixed computed 'color' values depending on property read order, including unresolved color-mix() results, which regressed in v29.0.2.
  • Fixed currentcolor border colors incorrectly becoming transparent when 'color' uses light-dark() or relative color syntax.
  • Fixed CSS calculations that reduce to a percentage incorrectly producing pixel values, which regressed in v30.0.0.
  • Fixed numeric font weights in the 'font' shorthand incorrectly setting 'line-height'.

  • Fixed exponentially slow reads of empty inherited CSS custom properties in deeply nested documents, and custom properties incorrectly inheriting past an initial reset. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning stale results after editing stylesheet declarations, selectors, or media queries, including in imported stylesheets.
  • Fixed selector matching and computed styles after changes to form control checkedness, indeterminacy, selection, values, and validity, including during form resets and canceled clicks.
  • Fixed computed styles for :focus, :focus-visible, :focus-within, and selectors containing them after focus changes, including inside focus and blur listeners. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing elements hidden by 'display', including through shadow hosts and slots, and elements excluded by shadow DOM slot assignment. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() throwing for elements without inline-style support, including XML and MathML elements.
  • Fixed a memory leak where stylesheet parsing retained the last parsed stylesheet's window after window.close().
  • Fixed memory growth from long-lived MutationObserver instances retaining bookkeeping for garbage-collected nodes. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed retained select.selectedOptions collections becoming stale after selection changes and form resets.
  • Fixed rejection of negative CSS sizing values, including for 'min-width', 'min-height', 'max-width', and 'max-height', which regressed in v30.1.0.
  • Fixed handling of deeply nested color-mix() expressions, including exceptions during color resolution. (@​asamuzaK)

Updates `sass` from 1.105.1 to 1.106.1
Release notes

Sourced from sass's releases.

Dart Sass 1.106.1

To install Sass 1.106.1, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

  • Fix a bug where an attribute selector with an empty value (such as [class=""]) would crash when serializing.

  • Don't crash when serializing a number with an empty unit. This is only possible through the JavaScript and Dart APIs or the embedded protocol.

Embedded Dart Sass

  • More robustly convert invalid value errors into PARAMS errors.

See the full changelog for changes in earlier releases.

Dart Sass 1.106.0

To install Sass 1.106.0, download one of the packages below and add it to your PATH, or see the Sass website for full installation instructions.

Changes

  • Don't normalize CSS escapes in statement contexts that can contain interpolation. For example, @f\6Fo is now emitted as written rather than normalized to @foo.

  • Fix a bug where quotes would be removed from attribute selector values that contained backslashes.

  • Fix invalid source spans that could cause crashes when encountering a syntax error in selectors or media queries that also contain escape sequences.

  • Fix a bug where the indented syntax parser would crash when parsing a file where the first statement was indented and appeared after the first line.

  • Fix a bug that could cause crashes when encountering errors or warnings in interpolations that contain patterns like // */.

  • Potentially breaking compatibility fix: CSS escape codes whose values are 0, for Unicode surrogates, or greater than the maximum allowed code point are now consistently normalized to U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER in expression contexts. Previously, in some cases these were instead normalized to the normalized form of the original escape sequence, which violates the principle that all escape sequences for identical values should be normalized the same way. In other cases, these would simply throw errors.

    As a special case, \0 on its own will continue to be normalized to \0 to support historical CSS hacks.

  • Potentially breaking bug fix: Throw an error for mixins and functions that have rest parameters which are the same as normal parameters. Previously, the positional parameters wouldn't be accessible and calling such a mixin or function with a named argument would crash the compiler.

  • Potentially breaking bug fix: Fix various cases where using a CSS escape code at the beginning of an identifier would change parsing behavior versus using the character directly.

  • Potentially breaking bug fix: When a number's unit is ambiguous with a numeric exponent, the unit is now serialized as an escape code rather than a literal e to avoid being interpreted as an exponent by CSS.

  • Potentially breaking bug fix: Don't parse a CSS escape code for U+45 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E or U+65 LATIN LOWERCASE LETTER E as an exponent in @keyframes percentage selectors.

  • Potentially breaking bug fix: Properly normalize underscores written as CSS escape codes in variable, mixin, and function names.

... (truncated)

data.body:
## Ziel

Ausfall- und Ersatzfolgen werden atomar mit ihren unveränderlichen Audit-Quellen gespeichert und aus diesen nach Neustart oder fehlgeschlagenem Folgeauftrag erneut verarbeitet. Kalenderfolgen sind gegen veraltete Origins gefenced; HTTP- und CLI-Pfade nutzen dieselbe Application-Orchestrierung.

## Umsetzung und Nachweis

- Auf Implementierungs-Head `4d16b65cc862bc215aca65db906794989c35f446` ergänzt ein Regressionstest den historischen Upgrade-Fall durch Migration 029: Watermark-Erfassung, Diagnose quellloser Alt-Audits, kein Replay vor dem Cutover, Replay einer neuen Quelle und idempotente Wiederholung nach erneuter Initialisierung.
- Die unabhängigen Code-, Application-Architektur- und Systemarchitektur-Delta-Reviews fanden keine neuen Befunde. GitHub Codex Code- und Security-Reviews auf `4d16b65c` fanden ebenfalls keine neuen Befunde; alle acht Review-Threads sind geschlossen.
- Alle ausgewählten CI-Prüfungen auf finalem PR-Head `a47ee9a555c9c7ae8f20baec6388a6d9082d379e` waren erfolgreich, einschließlich Backend, Admin-Socket-Integration, Container, Dokumentation, statischem Artefakt, CLI-Matrix, OpenAPI, CodeQL, Secrets, Workflow und Delivery. Nicht ausgewählte Frontend-, Infra-, Packaging-, Dependency-Audit- und manuelle Deployment-Jobs wurden übersprungen.
- Der Security-P2 zu wachsendem Calendar-Before-Image wurde behoben und sein Thread geschlossen. Neue unveränderliche Quellen speichern aktive Calendar-Generationen; stornierte Zeilen bleiben im Calendar-Projektionsspeicher und Allocator.

Gemerged am 25.10.2026 als `bfc5ed89d0f4fe045eaeb5f6488b1b11e88e2065`.

Closes #1158

repo.description: Vom Lehrling zum Gesellen: Verwaltung von IHK-Ausbildungsprüfungen
repo.name: lzug

data.body:
## Summary

Adds recursive backend package-boundary checks, rejects ORM/SQL leaks from public port annotations and representative runtime port values, tightens Application dependencies, introduces consumer ports for notification and absence workflows, and routes exam-day lifecycle orchestration through unit-of-work boundaries.

Round and day close/reopen validation consumes detached facts. Persistence owns transition writes and returns materialized values; Application coordinates cross-domain Assessment writes in the same UoW and publishes notification jobs after commit. Lifecycle Execution services no longer import SQLAlchemy, Sessions, Persistence models, or Presentation renderers. Export use cases return authorized projections, and FastAPI renders text exports after the UoW. Machine JSON remains unchanged.

Candidate terminal status validates committee authorization and round membership before applying the lifecycle lock. Absence replacement selection validates authorization and the lifecycle lock before Calendar preflight sync, then repeats the lock check in the writer transaction. AbsenceService consumes an Execution-owned port/UoW; SQLite Persistence materializes detached snapshots and performs lock checks, day mutation guards, and writes in the same writer transaction.

The direct post-commit Calendar/Notification path from Absence remains a documented migrations-free transition until dependent issue #1158. The maintainer confirmed it is outside #1085 acceptance and does not complete epic #1069.

Closes #1085

## Verification

- `mise exec -- task quality:backend:pr` passed on the code content at `b4edeb84`: 786 tests, 37 skipped; mypy, Ruff, and Black passed. Later commits changed documentation only.
- On final head `4585c600`, `mise exec -- task test:docs` passed (11 tests), and `git diff --check` passed.
- Two independent exact-head C3 reviews (Code and Application Architecture), against base `1f9d4792`, found no remaining findings.
- All active PR checks passed except `Build and validate static artifact`: its built-artifact linkcheck received HTTP 503 from GitHub for several existing `github.com/.../blob/...` links to unchanged frontend files. Two failed-job reruns reproduced the same external 503 class on other links; the latest retry had three 503 responses. No further retry is planned. The artifact build and browser/accessibility steps completed before the first linkcheck failure; the rerun stopped at the repeated linkcheck failure.

## Scope boundary

#1085 remains migrations-free. Versioned replay, the immutable follow-up source, durable Application claim/retry, and migration are tracked by dependent issue #1158. No schema or data migration is included here.

Die Backend-Taskbeschreibung nannte bisher alle durch unittest-Discovery gefundenen Tests „Unit-Tests“, obwohl ein Teil SQLite-Komponenten, FastAPI/HTTP oder Subprozess-/Socketgrenzen prüft. Der PR ordnet alle Testmodule genau einer Ebene zu, bietet gezielte Task-Einstiege und führt die Ebenen für den vollständigen PR-Testlauf parallel aus. Coverage verwendet weiterhin die vollständige gemeinsame Suite; kein Test oder CI-Gate entfällt.

Lokaler Nachweis auf macOS, Head `308884baf3e025e5fa2cb9e40de10d33ceb3bf8e`:
- `task backend:quality` bestanden: 741 Tests, 37 plattform-/binärbedingt übersprungen, 86 % Gesamtdeckung; vollständige Coverage-Suite lief unsharded in 110,4 s.
- `task backend:quality:pr` bestanden: Ruff, MyPy, Black und alle vier Ebenen.
- HTTP-Tier: 326 Tests auf drei vollständige, disjunkte Shards verteilt; lokal 29,8 s, 31,3 s und 38,7 s.
- Unit 77 Tests / 0,6 s; Component 268 / 21,6 s; Process 70 / 2,1 s, davon 37 übersprungen.
- `git diff --check` bestanden.

Linux-CI auf Ubuntu 24.04, derselbe Head:
- `task backend:quality:pr` erfolgreich in 108 s.
- Die HTTP-Shards liefen in 81,6 s, 84,2 s und 99,2 s; alle 326 Tests bestanden.
- Pull-Request-CI und Public-Site-Workflow erfolgreich.

Die frühere ungeteilte Linux-HTTP-Ebene dauerte 322,8 s.

## Summary

- Document why no common technical wrapper is warranted after #1083 moved HTTP contracts to the adapter boundary.
- Name the existing RuntimeAdmission, AdminSocket worker, RuntimeCoordinator operation, persistence and observability ownership boundaries and the behavior they preserve.
- Distinguish non-streamed command disconnects, which do not cancel the application worker, from failed streamed downloads, which unwind their lease with the stream.
- Pages and Wiki are unaffected because no operator-facing or operational contract changed.

No productive code changed: inspection found no remaining repeated admin, cleanup or event orchestration with a shared lifecycle contract. A wrapper would add indirection without consolidating behavior.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`
- `uv run --locked --extra dev python -m unittest discover -s tests/docs` (11 passed)
- `uv run --locked --extra dev python -m unittest backend.tests.test_admin_socket backend.tests.test_runtime backend.tests.test_runtime_adapters` (48 ran, 23 passed, 25 skipped)
- `uv run --locked --extra dev python -m docs.media.check` (passed)
- Independent code and application-architecture reviews at base `92fb0d611e558bee08d11c360f31e81976dcdb49` and final head `1c2c6611b7481469ba337e132721a022041e324f`; no findings.
- PR CI, CodeQL and GitHub code/security reviews passed at final head `1c2c6611b7481469ba337e132721a022041e324f`. The sole automated review finding was corrected and its outdated thread resolved.

`task docs` was attempted but its `docs:media:check` child invokes system Python 3.9 and fails parsing existing Python 3.10+ exception syntax; the same checker passed when invoked via the locked project `uv` environment.

Closes #1084

Updates `pydantic-settings` from 2.15.0 to 2.16.0
Release notes

Sourced from pydantic-settings's releases.

v2.16.0

Highlights

Breaking changes and behavior changes

  • Python 3.10 is no longer supported (#1003). pydantic-settings now requires Python 3.11+, since 3.10 reaches end of life this month. The tomli fallback is gone in favor of stdlib tomllib; the toml extra is kept as an empty extra so pip install pydantic-settings[toml] keeps working.
  • python-dotenv>=1.2.2 is now required (#971) to pick up the fix for CVE-2026-28684.
  • Aliases are ignored in every source when validate_by_alias=False (#1033). Env vars, secrets, CLI flags and defaults now use only field names, matching pydantic. An env var named after the alias is now ignored instead of raising extra_forbidden, and the CLI exposes --apple rather than --pomo.
  • validation_alias takes precedence over alias (#1038). When the two differ, values from JSON/YAML/TOML files and the CLI were silently ignored; they now load. CLI help lists the validation_alias flag first, and CliApp.serialize emits it.
  • CLI case-insensitivity only lowercases registered options (#1036). With case_sensitive=False, args after -- and those captured by CliUnknownArgs keep their case (-Xmx4G no longer becomes -xmx4g). Unrecognized options are now reported as typed (--NOPE instead of --nope).
  • JSON and YAML config files are read as UTF-8 by default (#955) instead of the locale encoding, completing the secrets-file fix from 2.15.0. json_file_encoding/yaml_file_encoding still override it.
  • Discriminated union defaults are partially updated again (#997). This reverts the 2.15.0 regression with nested_model_default_partial_update=True: the default is only dropped when the incoming value selects a different union member.

New features

  • Python 3.15 and pydantic 2.14 support (#1026, #1029, #1022). pydantic 2.14 broke CliApp.run and validate_by_alias=False handling; both are fixed.
  • Cached settings instances via Settings.settings_cached() and Settings.settings_clear_cache() (#952). These give you a process-local singleton per settings class without hand-rolling lru_cache wrappers. Calling the class directly still builds a fresh instance.
  • AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store source — AWSSystemsManagerSettingsSource (#941). It recursively reads every parameter under an ssm_path, with / mapping onto nested models. Install it with the new aws-systems-manager extra.
  • env_file_depth (#940) lets a relative env_file be found in parent directories, mirroring pyproject_toml_depth. This is useful when scripts run from a subdirectory of a monorepo. It defaults to 0, which keeps the current behavior.
  • CliVariadicArg for named variadic options (#949, #958). It accepts --param a b c in addition to repeated --param a --param b. Required fields need at least one value.

Bug fixes

CLI

  • CliApp.serialize output now round-trips through CliApp.run for enums, tuples, dates and Decimals (#988), explicit None values (#981), empty containers (#1008), CliVariadicArg values (#976) and populated CliUnknownArgs fields, which previously raised IndexError (#992).
  • Empty JSON arrays (--items []) now give an empty list instead of [''] (#994).
  • Tuples, frozenset, MutableSequence and other collection subtypes are now treated as repeatable/variadic options (#972), and so are named collection type aliases such as TypeAliasType('Addrs', list[IPvAnyAddress]) (#1032).
  • cli_exit_on_error=False is now honored in CliSubCommand parsers, which raise SettingsError instead of exiting (#977).
  • CliSubCommand aliases keep their case with case_sensitive=False (#989).
  • Each CliUnknownArgs field now receives only its own subcommand's leftover args (#1004).
  • CliApp.format_help no longer crashes when cli_prefix is set in model_config (#945).

Type aliases and parsing

  • Named union type aliases (TypeAliasType('V', list[int] | str)) now decode like their inline equivalents in env and dotenv sources, including under Optional, Annotated and custom validation aliases (#1006, #1030, #1041).
  • Resolving a named Annotated type alias no longer mutates shared FieldInfo metadata, which made validators run twice on subclasses or after model_rebuild() (#979).
  • A bare single-segment AliasPath('SOME_KEY') no longer tries to JSON-decode plain string values (#980).
  • collections.abc.Set/MutableSet/typing.AbstractSet fields now JSON-decode env values (#973).
  • A bare typing.Dict field with env_nested_delimiter no longer raises IndexError, which was a regression in 2.13.0 (#1009).
  • Case-insensitive matching now works for nested pydantic dataclasses (#1010).

Dotenv, secrets and config files

  • With extra='allow', a non-lowercase env_prefix is now stripped from dotenv extras (#959, #968).
  • secrets_case_sensitive=True is now honored on Windows (#1001).
  • An empty JSON config file is treated as an empty mapping instead of crashing (#947), matching YAML and TOML.
  • TOML table headers: ~ paths are now expanded when checking that the file exists (#1034), and an explicit toml_table_header=() now overrides the model config to read the file root (#1027).

Cloud sources

  • Azure Key Vault and GCP Secret Manager now honor env_parse_none_str (#1019, #1040).
  • Azure Key Vault: dash_to_underscore=True now works for nested model fields (#1025).
  • NestedSecretsSettingsSource now validates its specific constructor arguments (#975).

Updates `sqlalchemy` from 2.1.1 to 2.1.4
Release notes

Sourced from sqlalchemy's releases.

2.1.4

Released: October 7, 2026

orm

  • [orm] [bug] [regression] Fixed regression caused by #13333 where assigning a MetaData object to the metadata attribute of a mapped Declarative class, in order to place that class's Table in a MetaData collection other than that of the _orm.registry, would emit a warning that the attribute name metadata should be left reserved. The warning is now emitted only when the metadata attribute is assigned to an object other than a MetaData.

    References: #13659

engine

  • [engine] [bug] [regression] Fixed regression from the 1.4 series where the DBAPI cursor used for a compiled statement that returns no rows, which includes DDL constructs such as CreateTable and DropTable as well as the SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT and RELEASE SAVEPOINT statements emitted by _engine.Connection.begin_nested(), was not closed after execution, and was instead left to be released when garbage collected. The cursor is now closed immediately, as was the case in 1.3 and as is already the case for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and _sql.text() statements.

    This change is also backported to: 2.0.55

    References: #13640

  • [engine] [bug] Fixed issue in the _engine.Connection.execution_options.logging_token option where setting the value to None or another false value would raise AttributeError if a logging token had not already been established on that _engine.Connection, such as on a newly checked out connection, when the option was set at the _engine.Engine level, or when the token was reset to None more than once. Regression introduced in 2.0.30 as part of #11210.

    This change is also backported to: 2.0.55

    References: #13641

  • [engine] [bug] [regression] Fixed regression where iterating a Result directly would create reference cycles that prevented the Result along with the DBAPI

Updates `ruff` from 0.16.9 to 0.17.0
Release notes

Sourced from ruff's releases.

0.17.0

Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-09.

The executables in our macOS and Windows release archives and ruff wheels are now code-signed. macOS executables are signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. Windows executables have timestamped Authenticode signatures from Azure Artifact Signing. This enables verification of the release publisher and binary integrity, supports publisher-based allowlisting, and should reduce security warnings and antivirus false positives.

Breaking changes

  • Update the default and latest Python versions for 3.15 (#28792)

    Ruff now defaults to Python 3.11 instead of 3.10 when no Python version is configured through target-version or requires-python. When checking for syntax errors without a configured Python version, Ruff now defaults to Python 3.15 instead of 3.14.

  • Update the default rule set (#28786)

    Several of the flake8-datetimez rules (DTZ001, DTZ005, DTZ006, DTZ007, DTZ011, DTZ012, and DTZ901) are no longer enabled by default, while undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-usage (F406), which corresponds to a syntax error, is now enabled by default.

  • Update Rust crate quick-junit to 0.8.0 (#27295)

    JUnit output now uses a skipped attribute instead of disabled on <testsuite> elements and includes a skipped attribute on the root <testsuites> element.

  • [flake8-import-conventions] Add datetime as dt as a conventional alias (ICN001) (#28790)

  • Support Unicode dummy variable names (#28722)

    The default lint.dummy-variable-rgx now recognizes underscore-prefixed Unicode names, such as _次, as dummy variables.

  • Update to Unicode 17 (#21229, #28784)

    Ruff now uses Unicode 17 data for identifier normalization and named character escapes ("\N{...}").

  • Always show unsafe and display-only fixes in the CLI (#27810)

    The default full output format now shows unsafe fixes and suggestions requiring manual review, regardless of the unsafe-fixes setting. Actually applying unsafe fixes still requires explicit opt-in.

  • Remove the Python dependency from conda-forge builds (conda-forge/ruff-feedstock#361)

    The conda-forge build no longer depends on Python, now supports linux-riscv64, win-arm64, and linux-ppc64le platforms, and now includes shell completions. However, no longer depending on Python means that python -m ruff and import ruff will no longer work. Use ruff directly from PATH instead. PyPI installations and those from the standalone installer are unaffected.

  • Remove support for ruff-lsp (#28750)

    Support for ruff-lsp, the legacy Python language server deprecated in Ruff v0.9.5, has been removed. The Ruff VS Code extension now always uses the native language server; ruff.nativeServer is deprecated and ignored. See the migration guide.

Stabilization

The following rules have been stabilized and are no longer in preview:

  • lazy-import-mismatch (TID254)
  • lazy-import-immediately-resolved (TID255)
  • os-path-commonprefix (RUF071)

Release notes

Sourced from black's releases.

26.10.1

Highlights

This release fixes a security issue in Black's bundled GitHub Action. Repositories that use the action are encouraged to update to the latest version of Black immediately. This update is received automatically when using psf/black@stable, and is independent of the version of Black installed by the action.

When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from tool.black.required-version, it now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for black requirements in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now rejected. This issue has been registered as GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2; a CVE identifier is pending.

Stable style

data.body:
## Ziel

Verlagert HTTP-Ergebnis-, Fehler-, HATEOAS-, Payload- und Request-Verträge an den Adapterrand und entfernt die universelle ResourceRepository-Fassade aus der Produktionsanwendung. Kalenderansichten werden über Planning-, Identity- und Execution-Ports in einem gemeinsamen Read-Snapshot komponiert.

## Nachweis

- Finaler PR-Head: `bc0a1567a711b462f82d237cc4c572f38f92813d`; Squash-Merge nach `master`: `92fb0d611e558bee08d11c360f31e81976dcdb49` (gleicher Tree).
- [Finale PR-CI](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/39063949593) erfolgreich, einschließlich Backend, Container/Pester, Admin-Socket, OpenAPI, Dependency-Audit, CodeQL und Delivery-Verträgen.
- [Public-Site-Push-Lauf](https://github.com/lxndrp/lzug/actions/runs/39064568278) auf dem Merge-Commit erfolgreich; der manuell freizugebende Deploy-Job wurde übersprungen.
- C4-Abnahme: unabhängige Code-, Anwendungsarchitektur-, Systemarchitektur- und DevOps-Reviews des Umsetzungsstands sowie gezielte Follow-ups bis zum finalen Head; keine bestätigten offenen Befunde. Der frühere Demo-Import-Befund wurde behoben und der Review-Thread aufgelöst.
- Der Produktionsstart importiert Ressourcenmetadaten aus `backend.http_resources`; der nur für Entwicklung benötigte Schema-Validator in `backend.http_contract` bleibt außerhalb des Runtime-Importpfads.
- Pages/Wiki nicht betroffen: keine öffentliche oder Betriebsvertragsänderung.

Closes #1083

Updates `jdx/mise-action` from 5.0.1 to 5.1.2
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/mise-action's releases.

v5.1.2: mise_dir now sets MISE_DATA_DIR; auto_update handles a locked mise binary

The mise_dir input now also sets where mise installs tools, so those tools end up in the cache. With auto_update: true, the action no longer crashes on Windows when the mise binary is still in use.

Fixed

  • mise_dir now exports MISE_DATA_DIR. Before this release, mise_dir moved the mise binary and the cache path, but mise kept installing tools to ~/.local/share/mise. The saved cache didn't include the tools. On runners where ~/.local isn't writable, the step failed with EACCES: permission denied. When mise_dir is set, the action now exports MISE_DATA_DIR=<mise_dir>, so tools are installed into the directory that gets cached. If your workflow sets a different MISE_DATA_DIR, the mise_dir input overrides it. If mise_dir isn't set, nothing changes. mise's state directory (~/.local/state/mise) stays where it is. If that path also can't be written, set MISE_STATE_DIR yourself. (#672 by @​jdx, fixes #668) 
    - uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
  with:
    mise_dir: ${{ runner.tool_cache }}/mise/data
  • auto_update no longer crashes when it can't replace mise.exe. On Windows, the step used to fail with a bare EPERM: operation not permitted, unlink '…\mise.exe' if another process was still using the binary. Now, if version isn't pinned and the existing binary passes verification against its recorded version, the action prints a warning and continues with that version. In any other case, the step fails with a message that says the file is in use and how to fix it. A pinned version never quietly keeps an older binary. (#665 by @​jdx, fixes #664)

Documentation

  • The README explains how to use mise's MISE_ENABLE_TOOLS setting as a job-level allowlist. Unlike install_args, the allowlist applies to the action's install and to later mise commands. If jobs use different allowlists, add the value to a custom cache_key. (#667 by @​zeitlinger)
  • The Rust cache section is updated for mise 2026.9.2 and later, where mise install repairs a restored toolchain instead of leaving rustfmt missing. Swatinem/rust-cache now works alongside mise-managed Rust. (#670 by @​jdx)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.1.1...v5.1.2

v5.1.1: GitHub token is no longer exported to later steps by default

mise-action no longer exports its GitHub token as MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN to every later step in the job. A new persist_github_token input lets you turn that back on, or pass a different token to later steps. This changes the default behavior. If later steps need the token, see Breaking Changes below.

Fixed

  • The GitHub token now stays inside the action by default. Before this release, the github_token input (which defaults to ${{ github.token }}) was written to GITHUB_ENV as MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN. That let any later step read the token and call the GitHub API with the job's permissions, even if the step never asked for a credential. Now the token is set only for the mise-action step and the processes it starts. The action masks the token in logs. (#658 by @​jdx, reported in #657)

Added

  • persist_github_token input (default false). It takes one of three values:

    • false: the token stays inside the action.
    • true: the token the action used is exported to later steps. If env.MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN is already set, it takes precedence over github_token.
    • A token value: that token is exported to later steps instead, for example a read-only token. The action still installs tools with github_token, or with MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN if it's already set.

    Setting false doesn't clear a MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN that was already set at the job level or exported by an earlier step. (#658 by @​jdx)

Breaking Changes

Check your workflow if a later step needs MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN, such as mise shims, mise exec, mise run or lazy tool installs that call the GitHub API. Those steps no longer get the token automatically and may hit GitHub API rate limits. To get the old behavior back, opt in:

- uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
  with:
    persist_github_token: true

Or give later steps a separate token:

- uses: jdx/mise-action@v5

Updates `ruff` from 0.16.9 to 0.17.0
Release notes

Sourced from ruff's releases.

0.17.0

Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-09.

The executables in our macOS and Windows release archives and ruff wheels are now code-signed. macOS executables are signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. Windows executables have timestamped Authenticode signatures from Azure Artifact Signing. This enables verification of the release publisher and binary integrity, supports publisher-based allowlisting, and should reduce security warnings and antivirus false positives.

Breaking changes

  • Update the default and latest Python versions for 3.15 (#28792)

    Ruff now defaults to Python 3.11 instead of 3.10 when no Python version is configured through target-version or requires-python. When checking for syntax errors without a configured Python version, Ruff now defaults to Python 3.15 instead of 3.14.

  • Update the default rule set (#28786)

    Several of the flake8-datetimez rules (DTZ001, DTZ005, DTZ006, DTZ007, DTZ011, DTZ012, and DTZ901) are no longer enabled by default, while undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-usage (F406), which corresponds to a syntax error, is now enabled by default.

  • Update Rust crate quick-junit to 0.8.0 (#27295)

    JUnit output now uses a skipped attribute instead of disabled on <testsuite> elements and includes a skipped attribute on the root <testsuites> element.

  • [flake8-import-conventions] Add datetime as dt as a conventional alias (ICN001) (#28790)

  • Support Unicode dummy variable names (#28722)

    The default lint.dummy-variable-rgx now recognizes underscore-prefixed Unicode names, such as _次, as dummy variables.

  • Update to Unicode 17 (#21229, #28784)

    Ruff now uses Unicode 17 data for identifier normalization and named character escapes ("\N{...}").

  • Always show unsafe and display-only fixes in the CLI (#27810)

    The default full output format now shows unsafe fixes and suggestions requiring manual review, regardless of the unsafe-fixes setting. Actually applying unsafe fixes still requires explicit opt-in.

  • Remove the Python dependency from conda-forge builds (conda-forge/ruff-feedstock#361)

    The conda-forge build no longer depends on Python, now supports linux-riscv64, win-arm64, and linux-ppc64le platforms, and now includes shell completions. However, no longer depending on Python means that python -m ruff and import ruff will no longer work. Use ruff directly from PATH instead. PyPI installations and those from the standalone installer are unaffected.

  • Remove support for ruff-lsp (#28750)

    Support for ruff-lsp, the legacy Python language server deprecated in Ruff v0.9.5, has been removed. The Ruff VS Code extension now always uses the native language server; ruff.nativeServer is deprecated and ignored. See the migration guide.

Stabilization

The following rules have been stabilized and are no longer in preview:

  • lazy-import-mismatch (TID254)
  • lazy-import-immediately-resolved (TID255)
  • os-path-commonprefix (RUF071)

... (truncated)

Release notes

26.10.1

Highlights

This release fixes a security issue in Black's bundled GitHub Action. Repositories that use the action are encouraged to update to the latest version of Black immediately. This update is received automatically when using psf/black@stable, and is independent of the version of Black installed by the action.

When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from tool.black.required-version, it now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for black requirements in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now rejected. This issue has been registered as GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2; a CVE identifier is pending.

Stable style

  • Fix a long Jupyter notebook assignment magic (for example x = !ls -la) being wrapped in parentheses, which IPython can no longer run; such cells are now left unchanged (#5481)

Updates `mypy` from 2.3.1 to 2.4.0
Changelog

Sourced from mypy's changelog.

Mypy Release Notes

Next Release

Mypy 2.4

We've just uploaded mypy 2.4.0 to the Python Package Index (PyPI). Mypy is a static type checker for Python. This release includes new features, performance improvements and bug fixes. You can install it as follows:

python3 -m pip install -U mypy

You can read the full documentation for this release on Read the Docs.

Python 3.15 Support

Mypy 2.4 supports running on Python 3.15 and type checking most Python 3.15 features. This includes the new builtin sentinel type for sentinel values (PEP 661), which mypy now supports (see below for details). Lazy imports (PEP 810) and unpacking in comprehensions (PEP 798) are also supported. Closed TypedDicts (PEP 728) have been supported since mypy 2.2, but the extra_items TypedDict argument, also introduced in PEP 728, is still unsupported. Support for extra_items will be added in a future mypy release.

Native Parser Enabled by Default

Mypy now uses the new native parser by default. It's based on the Ruff parser, and it's significantly faster than the legacy parser, which uses the stdlib ast module. The native parser also has other benefits:

  • You can target newer Python versions and use recent Python syntax even when running mypy on an older Python version. For example, you can use --python-version 3.15 when running mypy on Python 3.14.
  • Stub files can use syntax that is newer than the target Python version. For example, stubs can use the PEP 695 generic class syntax (class Box[T]: ...) when running on or targeting Python 3.10.
  • Parallel type checking requires the native parser.

The legacy parser is still available through --no-native-parser, or native_parser = False in the config file (native_parser = false under [tool.mypy] in pyproject.toml). We are planning to remove the legacy parser in early 2027. If you run into a problem with the native parser, please report it on the issue tracker.

Bumps the codeql group with 2 updates in the / directory: [github/codeql-action/init](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) and [github/codeql-action/analyze](https://github.com/github/codeql-action). Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.2 to 4.39.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });

## Ziel

Entkoppelt Backup, Restore, Wartung, Diagnose und Backup-Empfänger-Audit von direktem SQLite-/Dateisystemzugriff in Operations. Operations besitzt die Speicher- und Wartungsverträge; Persistence implementiert sie. Bestehende Snapshot-, Mutations-, Restore-Aktivierungs- und Kompensationsgrenzen bleiben erhalten.

Closes #1082

## Nachweis

- `task backend:quality:pr`: erfolgreich auf dem Quellstand von `7c91bc4`; 734 Tests bestanden, 37 übersprungen. MyPy, Ruff und Black ebenfalls erfolgreich.
- Vier fokussierte Regressionstests zu Restore-Fehlerklassifikation, Rollback-Datenerhalt, Cleanup-Fehlervertrag und Dokument-Preflight bestanden.
- `task docs:test`: erfolgreich; 11 Tests bestanden.
- `task brand:check`: erfolgreich; 7 generierte Dateien reproduzierbar.
- `git diff --check`: erfolgreich.
- Vollständige PR-CI am Head `7c91bc4` erfolgreich, einschließlich Backend-Qualität, Admin-Socket-Integration, Dokumentation, CodeQL und Delivery-Prüfungen; Public-Site-Workflow ebenfalls erfolgreich.
- `task quality`: lokal durch den nicht erreichbaren Docker-Dienst blockiert. `pip_audit` meldete `multidict 6.7.1` (PYSEC-2026-4244, Fix ab 6.9.1); dieser PR ändert keine Abhängigkeiten.

## Unabhängige Reviews

Complexity-Evidenz aus Project #2: C4 – Systemic, P1, 40 h, für Issue #1082 am 2026-10-15 übergeben.

Code-, Application-, System- und DevOps-Reviews auf Head `7c91bc4` meldeten keine neuen Befunde. Automatischer Code- und Security-Review auf demselben Head abgeschlossen, ohne Befunde. Alle Inline-Threads sind geklärt.

## Umsetzung

- Dokumentfachlichkeit und Metadaten-/Inhaltsschnittstellen in ein consumer-owned `documents`-Modul verschoben; Filesystem und SQLite bleiben explizite Adapter.
- Operations besitzt die technische Dokument-Snapshot-Schnittstelle und portable Metadatenprojektionen; Persistence implementiert den Vertrag ohne Modulzyklus.
- Schreib-/Löschkompensation bleibt unter der Snapshot-Sperre; Streameigentum, Lesegrenze, Größen- und Medientypgrenzen sind festgelegt.
- Keine Schemaänderung und keine neue fachliche Ownership oder Autorisierung; die bestätigte Scope-Entscheidung steht in #1080.

## Nachweis

- `task backend:quality:pr` — erfolgreich: Lint, Typprüfung, Formatierung und 728 Backend-Tests (37 übersprungen).
- `task docs:test` — erfolgreich: 11 Tests.
- `git diff --check` — erfolgreich.
- Die separate breite lokale `task quality`-Prüfung war wegen fehlendem Docker-Daemon, fehlenden Frontend-Abhängigkeiten, dem bekannten Demo-Befund #1140 und dem lokalen Python-Aufruf des Media-Checks nicht vollständig erfolgreich. CI dieses PR-Kandidaten läuft vollständig.
- Keine Pages-/Wiki-Vertragsänderung erforderlich: betroffen sind interne Backend- und Entwicklerverträge, die in diesem PR aktualisiert sind.

Closes #1080

Bumps the python-security group with 1 update in the / directory: [multidict](https://github.com/aio-libs/multidict). Updates `multidict` from 6.7.1 to 6.9.1
Release notes

Sourced from multidict's releases.

6.9.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed the C extension reading freed memory on free-threaded builds when a list handed to :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.update, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.extend, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.merge or the :py:class:~multidict.MultiDict and :py:class:~multidict.CIMultiDict constructors, a [key, value] item inside any iterable handed to them, or a list tested with in against :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.items, is changed by another thread; a call that catches the list shrinking under it now raises :py:exc:RuntimeError -- by :user:rodrigobnogueira.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1437.

  • Fixed a data race on the free-threaded build where a retired hash table's reader count used relaxed atomics, letting a lock-free get()/getone()/ __getitem__() read race a concurrent free of that table. The reader-exit decrement and the drain's free check now use release/acquire ordering instead -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1481.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where two threads calling update(), merge(), or __setitem__() on the same key at the same time could lose the key entirely instead of just racing on which value wins. A decref of the replaced value could transiently suspend the writer's critical section, letting a second writer for the same key observe the first writer's in-progress entry as absent and, once both settled, mistake it for a stale duplicate and delete it. Every such decref is now deferred until the writer has released its critical section, so the window can no longer open. setdefault() had an unrelated instance of the same blind spot (it could insert a duplicate rather than recognizing an in-flight key), fixed alongside it -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1483.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where getall() and the items()/ keys()/values() equality path could raise KeyError or report a present, never-deleted key as missing. A concurrent update()/extend()/ __setitem__() call can have its critical section transiently suspended (a decref triggering a blocking allocator call) while an entry is marked as part of its own bookkeeping; a reader landing in that window used to treat the mark as "not found" instead of "still there, in flight" -- by :user:asvetlov.

Updates `jdx/mise-action` from 5.0.1 to 5.1.1
Release notes

Sourced from jdx/mise-action's releases.

v5.1.1: GitHub token is no longer exported to later steps by default

mise-action no longer exports its GitHub token as MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN to every later step in the job. A new persist_github_token input lets you turn that back on, or pass a different token to later steps. This changes the default behavior. If later steps need the token, see Breaking Changes below.

Fixed

  • The GitHub token now stays inside the action by default. Before this release, the github_token input (which defaults to ${{ github.token }}) was written to GITHUB_ENV as MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN. That let any later step read the token and call the GitHub API with the job's permissions, even if the step never asked for a credential. Now the token is set only for the mise-action step and the processes it starts. The action masks the token in logs. (#658 by @​jdx, reported in #657)

Added

  • persist_github_token input (default false). It takes one of three values:

    • false: the token stays inside the action.
    • true: the token the action used is exported to later steps. If env.MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN is already set, it takes precedence over github_token.
    • A token value: that token is exported to later steps instead, for example a read-only token. The action still installs tools with github_token, or with MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN if it's already set.

    Setting false doesn't clear a MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN that was already set at the job level or exported by an earlier step. (#658 by @​jdx)

Breaking Changes

Check your workflow if a later step needs MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN, such as mise shims, mise exec, mise run or lazy tool installs that call the GitHub API. Those steps no longer get the token automatically and may hit GitHub API rate limits. To get the old behavior back, opt in:

- uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
  with:
    persist_github_token: true

Or give later steps a separate token:

- uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
  with:
    persist_github_token: ${{ secrets.READ_ONLY_TOKEN }}

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.1.0...v5.1.1

v5.1.0: Tool version outputs, plugins input, and cached mise reuse

mise-action now reports the tool versions it installed as step outputs, can install mise plugins before tools, and can save the cache at the end of the job. Several caching fixes stop the action from downloading mise again on every run.

Added

  • Tool versions as step outputs. After install, the action runs mise ls --json --current and sets a versions output. This is a JSON object of the active, installed tools. Each tool maps to a list of {version, requested_version, install_path, source} entries. Each tool also gets its own output with its resolved version, such as steps.mise.outputs.node. A tool only gets its own output if its name is a valid output name and isn't cache-hit or versions. Names like npm:@scope/pkg appear only in versions. If the action can't read the versions, it prints a warning and the step still succeeds. (#655 by @​jdx) 
    - uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
  id: mise
- run: echo "node ${{ steps.mise.outputs.node }}"
  • plugins input. List plugins one per line as name or name url. Blank lines and # comments are ignored. The action runs mise plugins install -y for each one before mise install. Plugins that are already installed, for example restored from the cache, are left as they are. An unknown plugin fails the step. When plugins is set, its hash is added to the default cache key. Custom cache_key templates can use it as {{plugins_hash}}. If plugins is unset, existing cache keys don't change. (#656 by @​jdx) 
    - uses: jdx/mise-action@v5

... (truncated)

Updates `jsdom` from 30.1.1 to 30.1.2
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.1.2

  • Updated URLs to support Unicode v18.0.0 in internationalized domain names.
  • Reduced package size and memory use for CSS property definitions. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed severe slowdowns when building large DOM trees, including SVG charts with D3, which regressed in v30.1.0. (@​cmdcolin)
  • Fixed exponentially slow reads of empty inherited CSS custom properties in deeply nested documents, and custom properties incorrectly inheriting past an initial reset. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning stale results after editing stylesheet declarations, selectors, or media queries, including in imported stylesheets.
  • Fixed selector matching and computed styles after changes to form control checkedness, indeterminacy, selection, values, and validity, including during form resets and canceled clicks.
  • Fixed computed styles for :focus, :focus-visible, :focus-within, and selectors containing them after focus changes, including inside focus and blur listeners. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing elements hidden by 'display', including through shadow hosts and slots, and elements excluded by shadow DOM slot assignment. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() throwing for elements without inline-style support, including XML and MathML elements.
  • Fixed a memory leak where stylesheet parsing retained the last parsed stylesheet's window after window.close().
  • Fixed memory growth from long-lived MutationObserver instances retaining bookkeeping for garbage-collected nodes. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed retained select.selectedOptions collections becoming stale after selection changes and form resets.
  • Fixed rejection of negative CSS sizing values, including for 'min-width', 'min-height', 'max-width', and 'max-height', which regressed in v30.1.0.
  • Fixed handling of deeply nested color-mix() expressions, including exceptions during color resolution. (@​asamuzaK)

Release notes

Sourced from sqlalchemy's releases.

2.1.3

Released: October 2, 2026

orm

  • [orm] [bug] [regression] Fixed regression where columns delivered to a mapped class from an unmapped _orm.MappedAsDataclass mixin, or from a class decorated with _orm.unmapped_dataclass(), would not be placed in the _schema.Table in the order in which they were declared on the mixin; columns that had no dataclass default, such as a primary key column with no _orm.mapped_column.default, or which made use of _orm.mapped_column.default_factory, would be moved after the remaining columns of the mixin.

    References: #13634

sql

  • [sql] [bug] [regression] Fixed regression caused by the new implementation of ExecutableStatement.params() where parameter values established using this method would not be rendered when compiling the statement with the literal_binds compiler option, instead rendering NULL with a warning.

    References: #13635

2.1.2

Released: October 2, 2026

orm

  • [orm] [bug] [regression] Fixed regression caused by #5987 where the selectinload() loader strategy would ignore additional criteria present in the _orm.relationship.primaryjoin of a many-to-many relationship, such as a comparison against a column on the association table or on the parent table, loading related rows that should have been excluded. The omit_join optimization for many-to-many relationships is now only used when the primaryjoin consists solely of comparisons between the parent's primary key columns and the association table.

    References: #13626

Changelog

Sourced from mypy's changelog.

Mypy Release Notes

Next Release

Mypy 2.4

We've just uploaded mypy 2.4.0 to the Python Package Index (PyPI). Mypy is a static type checker for Python. This release includes new features, performance improvements and bug fixes. You can install it as follows:

python3 -m pip install -U mypy

You can read the full documentation for this release on Read the Docs.

This includes the new builtin sentinel type for sentinel values (PEP 661), which mypy now supports (see below for details). Lazy imports (PEP 810) and unpacking in comprehensions (PEP 798) are also supported. Closed TypedDicts (PEP 728) have been supported since mypy 2.2, but the extra_items TypedDict argument, also introduced in PEP 728, is still unsupported. Support for extra_items will be added in a future mypy release.

Native Parser Enabled by Default

Mypy now uses the new native parser by default. It's based on the Ruff parser, and it's significantly faster than the legacy parser, which uses the stdlib ast module. The native parser also has other benefits:

  • You can target newer Python versions and use recent Python syntax even when running mypy on an older Python version. For example, you can use --python-version 3.15 when running mypy on Python 3.14.
  • Stub files can use syntax that is newer than the target Python version. For example, stubs can use the PEP 695 generic class syntax (class Box[T]: ...) when running on or targeting Python 3.10.
  • Parallel type checking requires the native parser.

The legacy parser is still available through --no-native-parser, or native_parser = False in the config file (native_parser = false under [tool.mypy] in pyproject.toml). We are planning to remove the legacy parser in early 2027. If you run into a problem with the native parser, please report it on the issue tracker.

## Ziel

- Kalenderfachlichkeit liegt im eigenen `calendar`-Modul mit consumer-owned Identity-, Planning- und Persistenzverträgen.
- SQLite/ORM-Zugriff bleibt im konkreten Adapter; Serviceprojektionen und ICS/HTTP-Rückgaben bleiben typisiert und am jeweiligen Rand dargestellt.
- Vorhandene Feed-, Ereignis-, Generationen-, Autorisierungs- und Synchronisationsregeln einschließlich schreibender Leseabläufe und Round-Rollback bleiben erhalten.
- Keine Schemaänderung oder Änderung öffentlicher Transportverträge; keine Demo-/Betriebsänderung.

## Nachweis

+

+

+### 68.2 The 3-problem smoke verdict
+
+| Task | Pre-fix verdict | Post-R1+R2 verdict |
+|------|----------------|---------------------|
+| HumanEval/1 (separate_paren_groups) | FAIL | **FAIL (unchanged)** |

+- **R3** (Q4K → FP16) — published Qwen 88.4% may use FP16; Q4K loses 1-3pp on hard problems
+- **R4** (temperature sampling) — `temperature=0.2, samples=3, majority` smooths over single-token errors

data.message:
test(realizar): apr-book-ch* family — bind 5 falsifications at PARTIAL_ALGORITHM_LEVEL (covers 27 chapters × 5 = 135 gates)

Adds 5 generic algorithm-level verdict functions covering the uniform
falsification schema shared by all 27 apr-book-ch{01..27}-v1.yaml
contracts (APR-BOOK reference book Chapter 1 through Chapter 27) — 27
contracts × 5 conditions = 135 falsifier instantiations covered by one
module.

23 unit tests covering provenance pins, pass/fail bands per gate, history-
section legacy-name allowance, realistic full-chapter scenarios, family
coverage smoke across all 27 chapters.

| Local ID | Predicate | Verdict fn |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| FALSIFY-APRBOOK-001 | Example exit code == 0 | `verdict_from_book_example_exit` |
| FALSIFY-APRBOOK-002 | Every section cites ≥ 1 arXiv ID | `verdict_from_section_citations` |
| FALSIFY-APRBOOK-003 | No active legacy names (MOVED/migration/history allowed) | `verdict_from_no_legacy_in_book` |
| FALSIFY-APRBOOK-004 | apr oracle --explain agrees with chapter | `verdict_from_oracle_consistency` |
| FALSIFY-APRBOOK-005 | All assert!() in example pass | `verdict_from_assert_pass` |

## Five Whys

1. Why bind these gates? — 27 apr-book-ch* contracts each declare 5
   P0-severity unkeyed falsifications; rejecting a chapter is a hard
   ship-blocker, so algorithm-level pinning of the predicates prevents
   silent drift across chapter rewrites.
2. Why ONE module for ALL 27 chapters? — All 27 share an IDENTICAL
   schema (verified by inspection of ch01 + ch08 + ch27); they differ
   only in title/example/citation-list metadata. One module covers all
   135 instantiations with maximum leverage.
3. Why "vacuous Pass" for `verdict_from_section_citations(&[])`? — A
   chapter with no sections is caught by FALSIFY-APRPAGE-001 (page
   exists) and FALSIFY-APRPAGE-004 (sections listed), not by
   APRBOOK-002 which is specifically about citation density. Following
   the "single owning gate per regression class" invariant.
4. Why allow "history" / "migration" alongside "MOVED" for legacy-name
   contexts? — APR-BOOK is a reference book; chapters explicitly
   include historical context ("Pre-APR-MONO, …") and migration notes.
   Strict "MOVED"-only would force unnatural prose. Matching the same
   policy as apr-page-* family.
5. Why split assert!() failures (005) from example-exit (001) when both
   failure modes terminate the process? — assert!() failure exits 101
   (panic) but so does any unrelated panic. Splitting the verdict
   surfaces the regression class: "assertion failed" vs "I/O error /
   missing file / network timeout". Distinct verdicts mean the CI
   alarm names the actual bug.

Refs: contracts/apr-book-ch{01..27}-v1.yaml (27 contracts)

data.body: ### Motivation - Make the video/support/description area and comment surfaces visually match the supplied reference by adding stronger, paper-like shadows and white “note” cards. - Improve the subscribe CTA visual: use the owner-specified yellow (`#FFEA00`), better-center the bell icon and label, and replace the bell with a new inline SVG that fits the site iconography. - Make small visual fixes to separators and comment composer so the language/like separators are solid black and comment input/threads appear as white paper cards with avatars kept outside the white surface. ### Description - Added lifted drop-shadow styles to the featured video frame and the description card in `app/components/Hero.tsx` and to the support box in `app/components/playlist/SupportBox.tsx`. - Replaced and restyled the subscribe bell component and CTA in `app/components/SubscribeButton.tsx` to use `#FFEA00`, improved icon/text centering, and introduced a new inline SVG bell that matches the site style. - Changed thin vertical separators in the hero (like/dislike) and navbar (language switcher) to black in `app/components/Hero.tsx` and `app/components/Navbar.tsx`. - Wrapped the comment composer and each comment content block in white, card-like surfaces (border + shadow) while keeping avatars outside the white area in `app/components/comments/components/CommentComposer.tsx` and `app/components/comments/components/CommentItem.tsx`. - Updated the ready-ticket queue to record this owner UI polish work in `docs/tickets/ready/README.md`. ### Testing - `next lint` (run via `npm run lint` targeted at modified files) completed successfully with a pre-existing Next.js warning about an `` used for upload preview, which was accepted as informational. - Type-check (`npm run typecheck`) failed due to unrelated existing test/type issues elsewhere in the repo (tests under `tests/unit/...`), not caused by these UI-only changes. - Automated screenshot attempt with Playwright failed because the Chromium browser binaries are not installed in this environment, so visual QA was not captured automatically. ------ [Codex Task](https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/tasks/task_e_6a4448b91be88329b8ca2bb6642dae34)

data.body:
**关闭原因：已被 #396 覆盖（同一功能的重复实现）**

本 PR 与 #396 做的是同一件事：给「未绑定网盘时执行解绑」的空状态加上 CTA 按钮。#396 已通过门禁合入 `main`。

两者的差别，以及为什么选了 #396：

| | #396（已合并） | #383（本 PR） |
|---|---|---|
| `zh-CN.js` 文案 | 不改，沿用现有 | 改成「点击下方按钮或发送 /drive」 |
| 测试断言 | `Button.inline(STRINGS.system.btn_bind_drive, ...)` 精确匹配 | `buttons: expect.any(Array)` |

**#396 更优的原因**：

1. **不改文案** — 按钮出现后，「您可以发送 /drive 命令来绑定新的网盘」这句话本身仍然成立且准确，用户既能点按钮也能发命令。本 PR 把它改成「点击下方按钮或发送 /drive」，收益不明显，却和 #380 #391 #399 #401 #405 五个 PR 撞在同一批 key 上，制造冲突。**能不改文案就不改** —— 文案改动的冲突成本远高于收益。
2. **测试断言更强** — `expect.any(Array)` 只能证明「传了个数组」，按钮文案错了、callback data 错了、按钮顺序错了，测试都照样绿。#396 直接断言 `Button.inline(STRINGS.system.btn_bind_drive, Buffer.from("drive_select_type"))`，把按钮文案和回调标识一起锁住了。

**给后续工作的建议**：断言要锁住「会出错的那部分」。`expect.any(Array)` / `expect.anything()` 只应用在确实无法预知的值（时间戳、随机 ID）上；凡是可以写出确定值的地方，就写确定值。

> 
> 本 PR 与 #396 做的是同一件事：给「未绑定网盘时执行解绑」的空状态加上 CTA 按钮。#396 已通过门禁合入 `main`。
> 
> 两者的差别，以及为什么选了 #396：
> 
> | | #396（已合并） | #383（本 PR） |
> |---|---|---|
> | `zh-CN.js` 文案 | 不改，沿用现有 | 改成「点击下方按钮或发送 /drive」 |
> | 测试断言 | `Button.inline(STRINGS.system.btn_bind_drive, ...)` 精确匹配 | `buttons: expect.any(Array)` |
> 
> **#396 更优的原因**：
> 
> 1. **不改文案** — 按钮出现后，「您可以发送 /drive 命令来绑定新的网盘」这句话本身仍然成立且准确，用户既能点按钮也能发命令。本 PR 把它改成「点击下方按钮或发送 /drive」，收益不明显，却和 #380 #391 #399 #401 #405 五个 PR 撞在同一批 key 上，制造冲突。**能不改文案就不改** —— 文案改动的冲突成本远高于收益。
> 2. **测试断言更强** — `expect.any(Array)` 只能证明「传了个数组」，按钮文案错了、callback data 错了、按钮顺序错了，测试都照样绿。#396 直接断言 `Button.inline(STRINGS.system.btn_bind_drive, Buffer.from("drive_select_type"))`，把按钮文案和回调标识一起锁住了。
> 
> **给后续工作的建议**：断言要锁住「会出错的那部分」。`expect.any(Array)` / `expect.anything()` 只应用在确实无法预知的值（时间戳、随机 ID）上；凡是可以写出确定值的地方，就写确定值。

Understood. Acknowledging that this work is now obsolete as it has been superseded by #396, and stopping work on this task. I have reverted all my local workspace changes.
